measure-relationships.label: Benchmarks: The process compares results against the measure as an external reference.
Informs: The process uses the measure as an input.
Measures performance: The process tracks the measure as a result of the business.

measures.definition: Renewables and natural gas liquids (NGL) market prices used in planning: renewable feedstocks, renewable fuels and their credits, and NGLs.
measures.label: Additional Market Prices (Renewables, NGLs)

measures.definition: A future capability for ad hoc trends of plan data and a chatbot over the planning database.
measures.label: Business Planning Data Trends (Ad Hoc / Chatbot)

measures.definition: Open capital project evaluations against their due dates.
measures.label: Capital Projects Evaluation

measures.definition: Benchmark crack spreads: the market value of products made from a set ratio of crude, less the crude's price.
measures.label: Crack Spreads Pricing

measures.definition: Crude oil benchmark prices and differentials, with related futures (natural gas, heating oil, RBOB).
measures.label: Crude Market Pricing

measures.definition: Fresh crude charged to the crude units as a share of crude capacity, for one refinery and month.
measures.label: Crude Utilization

measures.definition: A screen of each crude's breakeven value from the planning model against its delivered price, by refinery, to pick incremental barrels for a full evaluation.
measures.label: Crude Value to Breakeven

measures.definition: The submitted mid-term plan for a month compared with the same month's average over prior years, by product (crude, gasoline, diesel, jet).
measures.label: Current Plan vs. Historical Averages (Crude, Gas, Diesel, Jet)

measures.definition: Actual sales less forecast sales for the period, against the plan version named.
measures.label: Demand vs. Forecast

measures.definition: Benchmark distillate and jet spot prices at named hubs.
measures.label: Distillate Market Pricing

measures.definition: Distillate produced (ULSD, kerosene, jet) as a share of crude and feed charged.
measures.label: Distillate Yield

measures.definition: Distribution costs, excluding depreciation and amortization, per barrel of net refinery throughput; mostly long-term agreements with MPLX.
measures.label: Distribution Costs per Barrel

measures.definition: Benchmark gasoline spot prices at named hubs.
measures.label: Gasoline Market Pricing

measures.definition: Gasoline produced (finished and blendstock) as a share of crude and feed charged.
measures.label: Gasoline Yield

measures.definition: Total product moved between regions on named segments, by product and mode.
measures.label: Interregional Volume Totals

measures.definition: Critical planning activities and meetings against their due dates.
measures.label: Key Activity Tracker

measures.definition: The margin given up because of planned turnaround downtime.
measures.label: Lost Margin from Turnarounds

measures.definition: Reported R&M margin as a share of the R&M Margin Indicator: how much of the benchmark margin was realized.
measures.label: Margin Capture

measures.definition: Volume moved by barge and vessel as a share of available marine capacity.
measures.label: Marine Utilization

measures.definition: Marketing's results against the marketing plan.
measures.label: Marketing Performance vs. Plan

measures.definition: Mid-term plan submissions against their due dates.
measures.label: MTP: Plan Submission

measures.definition: Each NGL product's balance at the refinery (opening, production, consumption, transfers) compared with planned purchases and make.
measures.label: NGL Commodities (Plan, Consumption, Transfers)

measures.definition: Actual opening inventory against the planned opening level for the next month.
measures.label: Opening Inventory vs. Plan

measures.definition: Pipeline throughput as a share of pipeline capacity, by distribution node and material.
measures.label: Pipeline Utilization

measures.definition: A summary of the largest plan changes and the economic drivers behind them.
measures.label: Plan Overview and Key Changes

measures.definition: Planned turnaround and major maintenance costs, expensed as incurred, per barrel of net refinery throughput.
measures.label: Planned Turnaround Costs per Barrel

measures.definition: The difference between two chosen market markers over time.
measures.label: Price Comparison

measures.definition: Total clean product output by refinery over the plan horizon.
measures.label: Production Make (Clean Products)

measures.definition: A notification when a refinery sets a new clean products production rate record.
measures.label: Production Rate Records

measures.definition: MPC's hypothetical R&M margin built from market data and operational guidance, posted monthly.
measures.label: R&M Margin Indicator

measures.definition: MPC's Refining & Marketing margin (sales revenue less the cost of refinery inputs and purchased products) per barrel of net refinery throughput.
measures.label: R&M Margin per Barrel

measures.definition: Refining operating costs, excluding planned turnaround and depreciation and amortization, per barrel of throughput.
measures.label: Refining Operating Costs per Barrel

measures.definition: A future view of plant status across the region, combining operations notes with unit performance.
measures.label: Regional / Site Monitoring

measures.definition: MPC's annual cash bonus Adjusted EBITDA per barrel of total throughput, as a percentile against a peer group.
measures.label: Relative Adjusted EBITDA per Barrel of Total Throughput

measures.definition: MPC's Refining EBITDA per barrel of total throughput for each region, ranked against the same regions of U.S. refining peers.
measures.label: Relative Refining Margin per Barrel by Region

measures.definition: A trend of rack sales and purchase statuses from marketing, showing statuses held for more than a week.
measures.label: Sales/Purchases Status Control

measures.definition: Actual purchases less forecast purchases for the period, against the plan version named.
measures.label: Supply vs. Forecast

measures.definition: The volume of swing streams and where they are routed, as they shift distillate and gasoline make.
measures.label: Swing Stream Disposition

measures.definition: A list of turnaround activities planned for the next four months, by refinery.
measures.label: TAR Activities Tracker

measures.definition: A process unit's throughput as a share of its constrained capacity, for one refinery.
measures.label: Unit Utilization

measures.definition: An alert raised when a distribution-plan input table changes by more than a set share from the week before.
measures.label: WoW Variances on DPO Input Tables

The downstream business function that creates, manages, and optimizes the commercial value of petroleum products and services through market strategy, customer and channel management, supply and trading, commercial planning and scheduling, pricing, sales, and order-to-cash activities.
Planning And Optimization Includes Processes Such As Demand Forecasting, Local And Regional Optimization, Backcasting And Inventory Management Across The Value Chain.
Demand forecasting processes for commercial planning across the value chain.

Develop, agree, and publish the recurring product demand forecast that downstream commercial planning runs on — expected demand by product, market, location, and period — by combining a statistical baseline with customer input and market intelligence, and monitor forecast performance so the published forecast remains a reliable planning basis.

Prepare and validate the reference data and demand history that each forecast cycle depends on — product and market hierarchies, customer and location groupings, units of measure, and the historical demand series cleansed of outliers and one-off distortions — so the statistical baseline is built from accurate, planning-consistent inputs.

terms.definition: Generate the objective statistical baseline forecast of product demand from cleansed history and demonstrated demand drivers, selecting and tuning forecasting methods by product and market segment before any judgmental input is applied.

Develop and maintain the short-term product supply schedule for the primary distribution network — deciding which products move between refineries, terminals, and supply points, in what quantities and sequence over the coming days and weeks — so the approved regional plan is translated into an executable movement program.

Produce the rolling days-to-weeks network supply plan that bridges the approved regional plan and daily execution — projecting stock, demand, production, and movements by location and product, and setting the movement quantities and timings the schedule will execute.

Identify schedule imbalances that cannot be resolved with the company's own supply — surpluses to place or shortfalls to cover — and coordinate with Supply And Trading to request, evaluate, and incorporate the purchases, sales, or exchanges that balance the short-term schedule.

Schedule and administer the primary distribution movements that execute the product schedule — nominating volumes to pipelines, vessels, rail, and terminals, administering load and discharge events, and tracking movements to closure — so scheduled product arrives where the plan requires, fully documented.

Prepare, submit, and manage volume nominations to pipelines, vessels, rail, and terminal operators — matching the short-term schedule to each carrier's cycles, batch specifications, and deadlines, and managing confirmations, revisions, and allocations through the cycle.

Administer the loading of scheduled shipments at refineries and terminals — authorizing the lifting, confirming loaded quantities and quality documentation, and capturing the load into movement and inventory records — so each shipment leaves accounted for and per schedule.

Track scheduled movements from load to discharge — monitoring progress against the schedule, maintaining in-transit inventory visibility by movement, and updating scheduling and inventory records as movements progress — so the network always knows what is en route, where, and when it will arrive.

Administer the discharge of arriving shipments — confirming received quantities and quality documentation, reconciling discharged against loaded volumes to surface in-transit gains and losses per movement, and closing the movement in scheduling and inventory records.

The capability to govern, measure, reconcile, control, position, replenish, and account for petroleum feedstocks, intermediates, and refined products across the downstream network, including their quantity, quality, location, ownership, entitlement, identity, and availability.

Establish and maintain the policy governing crude and feedstock inventories — target and minimum operating levels, safety and strategic stock requirements, tankage and segregation rules, and review triggers — so feedstock supply to refineries is protected at an efficient working-capital cost.

Manage inventory that must be tracked by lot or batch identity — such as specialty products, additives, and quality-certified stock — preserving batch identity, certificates, and traceability from receipt through storage to issue.

Manage company inventory held in third-party storage facilities — leased tankage, throughput agreements, and commercial storage — administering capacity entitlements, monitoring stock positions and operator statements, and managing performance against the storage agreements.

Monitor and control actual and projected inventory positions for finished products and intermediates: identify operating-limit, availability, ownership, quality, location, and balance exceptions, coordinate timely response, and provide reliable current-position information to planning and operational stakeholders.

Compare the quantities measured at each end of a movement or held in storage, find the losses and gains, and settle the imbalances, for every movement by pipeline, marine, rail, truck and storage, including transfers of intermediates between refineries.

Establish and maintain the policy governing intermediate and blendstock inventories held between process units and blending — target working levels, segregation and quality-protection rules, and review triggers — so conversion and blending operations are decoupled without trapping excess working capital.

Establish and maintain the policy governing finished-product inventories across refineries and the distribution network — target and minimum operating levels, safety stock by product and location, brand and quality segregation rules, and review triggers — so customer supply reliability is protected at an efficient working-capital cost.

Establish the measured physical quantity of crude, intermediate, and product inventory across the network — from tank gauging, metering, and vessel and pipeline measurements converted to standard conditions — so book stock, reconciliation, and planning rest on accurate physical positions.

Reconcile book inventory against measured physical inventory by location and material, quantify and classify gains and losses, investigate variances beyond tolerance, and post agreed corrections so stock records remain accurate and losses are made visible.

Manage product held under consignment arrangements — stock positioned at a customer's or partner's site, or held for a third party at company sites, that remains the consignor's property until drawn — tracking positions, draws, and settlement triggers so ownership and stock records stay correct on both sides.

Manage company stock held commingled with other owners' fungible product in shared tanks, pipelines, and terminals — tracking each party's ownership share, quality basis, and allocated gains and losses under the operative agreements — so the company's entitlement in shared stock is always known and defensible.

Manage the re-designation of existing inventory between brand, grade, or specification categories — such as converting unbranded stock to branded through additive treatment, or regrading product that qualifies against a different specification — so stock records, quality status, and documentation reflect what the product now is.

Plan and trigger the replenishment of finished-product stock points across the distribution network — determining when and how much to resupply each terminal and depot within inventory policy and the approved plan — so locations stay between minimum and maximum operating levels without emergency movements.

Manage the delivery of products from terminals and depots to retail sites, commercial customers, and other end-delivery points — generating delivery orders for managed sites, scheduling vehicles and routes, and monitoring delivery performance — so site and customer demand is met reliably at efficient delivery cost.

Create the delivery orders that feed secondary distribution scheduling — deriving replenishment needs for managed retail sites and customer tanks from stock readings, consumption forecasts, and agreed service levels, and converting them into deliverable orders with quantities and windows.

Build and maintain the daily secondary delivery schedule — assigning orders to vehicles, compartments, routes, and time windows within fleet, driver, site-access, and product-segregation constraints — to meet required delivery windows at efficient fleet utilization and cost.

Maintain the reference data, constraints, and operating parameters used for secondary-distribution scheduling — including sites, tanks, vehicles, compartments, drivers, routes, access windows, product-compatibility rules, and scheduling parameters — so generated orders and delivery schedules reflect the current operating network.

Measure and report secondary distribution execution against the issued delivery schedule — delivery reliability, fleet utilization, and cost efficiency at agreed levels — investigating recurring shortfalls and feeding improvements back into order generation, scheduling, and the scheduling basis.

Develop the commercially optimal refinery production plan — selecting crude and feedstock intake, refinery operating modes, unit-throughput targets, product yield and quality targets, and production horizons — to fulfill commercial commitments and maximize margin within feasible refinery, supply, inventory, product-specification, and contractual constraints.

Translate the current production schedule into each day's refinery execution basis — updating the day's scheduling instructions and commitments, confirming the schedule-level resources the day depends on, and closing the daily production accounting balance — so the refinery works each day from a current, feasible, accounted-for scheduling basis.

Maintain and issue the approved daily production-schedule instructions — dated campaign commitments, production and movement requirements, product priorities, planning assumptions, and approved schedule changes — so the refinery's operating teams receive a current, traceable scheduling basis.

Assign and confirm the schedule-level shared resources each day's plan depends on — tankage assumptions, movement and rack windows, berth and loading slots, and other capacity the schedule reserves — so the daily scheduling basis is physically feasible before it is issued.

Close the refinery's daily production balance — reconciling measured feed receipts, unit charges and yields, blending, shipments, fuel and loss, and inventory changes into an accounted material balance — and actualize production against the schedule so planning, scheduling, and backcasting run on verified actuals.

Develop and maintain the refinery production schedule that implements the approved monthly plan — sequencing campaigns, schedule-level unit commitments, blends, and movements over the scheduling horizon, managing schedule exceptions, and coordinating the interfaces the schedule depends on — so the plan becomes a current schedule that provides the approved basis for refinery execution.

Create, maintain, and retire the reference and parameter data the production scheduling model depends on — unit capacities and constraints, product and recipe definitions, transition and changeover rules, tankage parameters, and scheduling calendars — so scheduling results remain accurate and reproducible.

Review and maintain the production wheel — the recurring sequence of product campaigns — and each campaign's run length, balancing transition losses and changeover costs against inventory, demand coverage, and unit constraints, so the schedule is built on an economically sound campaign structure.

Trading management consists of processes performed in the front office such as forecasting, pre-trade analysis, managing counterparty credit and contracts, executing and capturing trades.

The front-office capability to assemble and maintain a forward commercial view of supply, demand, generation, renewables, market conditions, and revenue, and to identify how the asset portfolio can be used commercially within approved plans and constraints.

Receive and incorporate the refinery production plans and schedules into the trading forward view — validating completeness, translating volumes into tradable supply by product, location, and period, and refreshing the view as plans and schedules change.

Receive the published demand forecast and incorporate it into the trading forward view — validating the version, translating product, market, and period detail into the granularity trading uses, and refreshing trading assumptions when a new version publishes.

Develop and maintain a forward view of renewable-fuel volumes, renewable-energy output or procurement, compliance obligations, and associated program-specific environmental attributes or credits — such as Renewable Identification Numbers where applicable — so commercial, trading, and compliance stakeholders can anticipate expected shortfalls, surpluses, and deadlines.

Assess and optimize the commercial use of approved asset flexibility — including storage, transportation and terminal capacity, supply commitments, exchanges, and generation availability — against market conditions, identifying and valuing opportunities and providing recommendations to approved trading strategies within established plans and constraints.

Project the trading organization's expected economics — projected trading revenue, gross margin, and economic exposure from current positions, planned flows, the forward view, and market prices — so management and strategy decisions rest on a current forward-looking outlook.

Receive and incorporate power generation forecasts — from company cogeneration and any contracted or merchant generation — into the trading forward view, validating them and translating expected generation into tradable positions by period.

Administer trading counterparties and commercial agreements through their lifecycle — onboarding and maintaining counterparty records; establishing, maintaining, terminating, and novating master agreements, standing agreements, and relevant transaction frameworks; managing specialized agreement types; and monitoring contractual obligations — so trading occurs with authorized counterparties under current, governed terms.

Coordinate onboarding of a prospective trading counterparty by collecting required legal-entity, tax, settlement, and commercial documentation; initiating and recording required compliance, sanctions/KYC, legal, and credit clearances through their accountable owners; and creating the authorized counterparty and settlement records once required approvals are complete.

Administer storage and throughput contracts through their life — recorded capacity, injection and withdrawal rights, fee structures, amendments, and renewals — so storage deals, inventory administration, and settlement operate against current, correct contract terms.

Monitor active agreements against their terms — tracking obligations, commitments, expiries, renewal windows, and utilization against contracted volumes and service levels — surfacing issues to the responsible owners before they become breaches or lapses.

Maintain active counterparty records through their life — processing changes to legal identity, ownership, settlement details, and documentation, keeping records synchronized with credit and compliance status, and periodically reconfirming record accuracy.

Coordinate the administrative counterparty offboarding or transfer — confirming that affected positions, agreements, collateral, payment instructions, and reporting responsibilities have been closed, settled, transferred, or queued for legally effective novation — and deactivate or transition counterparty records with preserved history.

Administer the counterparty, agreement, trade-record, and obligation consequences of merger, acquisition, divestiture, restructuring, or legal-entity change events affecting either a trading counterparty or the company's own trading entities — coordinating, recording, and operationalizing the resulting novations, assignments, renamings, and record transfers once required legal documentation and approvals are complete.

Establish new trading agreements in the contract record — capturing negotiated terms, verifying required approvals and legal review are complete, linking the agreement to its counterparty and settlement basis, and activating it — so transactions governed by the agreement can be captured, confirmed, actualized, and settled against controlled terms.

Maintain active agreements through their life — processing approved amendments, extensions, and renewals, keeping recorded terms synchronized with what the parties have agreed, and managing agreement documentation and versions — so the contract record always reflects the operative agreement.

End or transfer an agreement in a controlled way — confirming obligations under it are fulfilled, settled, or queued for legally effective novation, executing the administrative termination or transfer steps, and closing the agreement record with its history preserved.

Administer crude and condensate lease purchase contracts — first-purchase arrangements at the lease or wellhead — through their life: recorded terms, price and deduction bases, division-of-interest references, amendments, and renewals, so lease purchases actualize and settle against current, correct contract terms.

Administer contracts with pipeline, marine, rail, and truck carriers through their life — recorded rates, capacity commitments, service terms, amendments, and renewals — so transportation deals, nominations, and freight settlement operate against current, correct carrier terms.

Perform the controlled pre-trade analysis, authorization, and post-execution recording of trades in the trading system — capturing complete commercial, operational, and regulatory terms by deal type and submitting required creation-data reports — so authorized transactions are available to confirmation, risk, actualization, settlement, and accounting processes.

Evaluate a prospective trade before execution — its economics, strategy fit, credit and limit headroom, operational feasibility where applicable, and regulatory treatment — so the trader and approver see the deal's value and consequences before committing the company.

Determine whether an executed swap or other transaction is reportable under an applicable trade-reporting regime and, where the organization is the reporting counterparty or has delegated reporting responsibility, submit required creation data to the designated registered swap data repository within applicable deadlines; correct errors and retain required reporting evidence.

Record executed power transmission deals — transmission service, capacity, and congestion-related rights, with path, quantity, period, and charges — so transmission positions and obligations are represented from execution onward.

Secure the approvals a trade requires before execution — verifying the trader's authority under the delegation of authority, escalating deals beyond that authority, and documenting each approval — so every executed trade is traceably authorized.

Record executed physical purchases and sales of crude, feedstocks, and products completely and promptly — counterparty, product and quality, quantity, price and pricing basis, delivery terms, location, period, and title-transfer terms — linked to book and strategy, so the trade record is available to confirmation, risk, actualization, and settlement.

Record exchange-executed futures and listed-options trades with contract, delivery month, quantity, price, account, clearing-broker, and allocation details; validate captured execution data against available execution and broker messages; and resolve trade-capture exceptions so the trading record reflects the executed cleared position.

Record executed storage and throughput deals — facility, capacity, injection and withdrawal rights, fees, and period — so capacity positions, obligations, and costs are represented in the trading system from execution onward.

Record executed purchases, sales, and transfers of program-specific environmental instruments — such as RINs, RECs, and emissions allowances — with program, vintage, quantity, price, and compliance-period detail, so instrument positions are accurate from execution onward.

Record executed over-the-counter derivative trades — swaps, options, and other bilateral instruments, with underlying index, fixed and floating terms, notional quantity, tenor, and counterparty — flagging reportable transactions, so financial positions and obligations are accurate from execution onward.

Record executed structured and non-standard transactions — multi-leg, embedded-optionality, tolling, prepay, and similar bespoke deals — decomposing them into capturable components so their positions, risks, and obligations are fully represented rather than approximated.

Record executed transportation capacity deals — pipeline capacity, vessel charters, railcar commitments, and trucking capacity, with route or path, capacity, period, and rates — so transport positions, obligations, and costs are represented from execution onward.

Develop, approve, and steward the trading strategies the front office runs — defining each strategy's objective, markets, instruments, and horizon, aligning it with approved authorities and risk limits, reviewing performance, and adjusting or retiring strategies as conditions change.

Confirmations and Risk management consists of processes performed in the middle office to minimize risk of losses in the trading book due to change in market conditions i.e. commodity prices, interest rates, credit spreads, foreign-exchange rates. Middle office is responsible for managing confirmations, scenario modelling and price forecasting.

The capability to control counterparty credit risk in trading — assessing counterparty creditworthiness, setting and maintaining credit limits, administering credit support and margin, measuring exposure, analyzing portfolio credit risk, monitoring positions against limits, and reporting the credit risk picture — so credit losses are anticipated, bounded, and visible before they happen.

Assess a counterparty's creditworthiness — at onboarding, on a periodic cycle, and on trigger events — analyzing financial statements, ratings, ownership and support structures, payment behavior, and qualitative factors, and assigning or updating the internal credit assessment that limits and monitoring run on.

Establish, maintain, publish, and adjust credit limits for trading counterparties and counterparty groups — based on approved credit assessments, risk appetite, exposure methodology, and credit-support arrangements — administer documented temporary-excess and exception decisions under delegated authority, and reduce, suspend, or withdraw limits when deterioration or policy triggers require it.

Administer contractual credit support both held and posted — cash collateral, securities, letters of credit, guarantees, and other eligible security, with their haircuts, thresholds, independent amounts, and substitutions — calling, receiving, returning, valuing, and reconciling credit support under the applicable arrangements, so credit exposure is secured to the extent the agreements require.

Calculate current and, where required by approved methodology, potential future credit exposure for each counterparty and group — aggregating trading positions, mark-to-market values, delivered-but-unpaid and other settlement-cycle exposures, and applicable netting, collateral, and credit-support effects — so limits, monitoring, and credit support run on a defensible exposure number.

Administer margin obligations for cleared and other applicable margined positions — receiving, validating, forecasting, and issuing or responding to margin calls as applicable, reconciling margin balances against CCP, exchange, broker, and counterparty statements, and escalating failed or disputed calls — so margin obligations are met and margin held matches what positions require.

Analyze credit risk at portfolio level — concentrations, stress and scenario impacts, default-likelihood signals, and correlation effects such as wrong-way exposure — so appetite, limits, and mitigation decisions rest on more than single-counterparty views.

Continuously watch counterparty credit — exposures against limits, breach detection and aging, and early-warning signals from ratings, news, payment behavior, and market indicators — escalating breaches and deterioration per policy and triggering reassessment where warranted.

Produce governed internal credit-risk reports — exposures, limit utilization, breaches, credit-support and margin positions, and concentrations, at agreed cadences and levels for management and committees — and provide controlled inputs to applicable external or regulatory reporting through their accountable owners, so the credit risk picture is current, consistent, and decision-ready.

Independently confirm and match executed trades with counterparties by generating, receiving, validating, documenting, modifying, reporting, and resolving discrepancies in trade confirmations, so the organization and its counterparty have evidenced agreement on the applicable trade terms.

Produce and dispatch outgoing trade confirmations from captured deal records — using the templates and terms of the governing agreement — and match incoming counterparty confirmations or equivalent contractual acknowledgements against the captured deal record, using the applicable product, agreement, and confirmation standards, chasing unconfirmed trades within applicable timeliness requirements.

Maintain the confirmation documentation basis — approved templates and standard wording aligned to governing agreements, the archive of dispatched and matched confirmations, and the evidence trail that shows what was agreed and when — so confirmations are consistent, current, and provable.

Coordinate the confirmation-side processing of agreed post-execution changes to a trade — including amendments, allocations, partial terminations, and early terminations — by validating counterparty agreement, initiating or validating the required controlled trade-record update, re-confirming revised terms, and triggering applicable lifecycle reporting.

Report confirmation and lifecycle events for reportable transactions under an applicable trade-reporting regime — submitting required continuation data for amendments, terminations, and other post-execution events to the designated registered swap data repository within applicable deadlines, where the organization holds reporting responsibility — correcting errors and retaining reporting evidence.

Resolve confirmation mismatches and disputes — logging discrepancies between the capture record and the counterparty's confirmation, investigating against execution evidence, agreeing the correct terms with the counterparty, and driving the resolution into the records and any required re-reporting.

The capability to independently measure, control, monitor, analyze, and report market risk in the trading book by governing risk-book structures, delegated authority, market-data inputs, valuations, limits, control cycles, positions, profit and loss, scenarios, and risk reporting.

Establish and maintain the governed trading-book and portfolio hierarchy used for risk aggregation, valuation, position control, and P&L reporting — defining risk-reporting book attributes, responsible owners, aggregation relationships, and effective-dated changes — and keep trading, risk, and reporting systems aligned to it.

Monitor adherence to the organization's own market-risk policies and control framework — mandate and delegation-of-authority adherence, control-cycle completion, exception-procedure use, and policy-required documentation — surfacing violations and control gaps to the accountable owners.

Define, maintain, and run the market-risk scenario and stress set — historical and hypothetical market shocks, commodity and basis stresses, and event scenarios — quantifying their P&L and risk impacts so the organization knows what adverse markets would do to the book before they happen.

Analyze market risk beyond the standard measures — backtesting the measures against outcomes, analyzing model behavior and measure limitations, investigating risk concentrations and emerging exposures, and developing analytical improvements — recommending changes to methodologies, limits, and controls.

Produce governed internal market-risk reports — measures, limit utilization, breaches, scenario results, positions, and P&L, at agreed cadences for management and committees — and provide controlled inputs to applicable external or regulatory reporting through their accountable owners.

Source, construct, validate, and publish the volatility and correlation parameters that option valuation and risk measurement depend on — by commodity, location, and tenor per approved methodology — so valuations and measures rest on governed market parameters, not ad hoc inputs.

Produce and control the official valuations of the trading book — marking positions to market or, where approved, to model per approved methodology from the official curves and parameters, applying approved valuation adjustments, investigating exceptions, and publishing the valuations that P&L, risk, exposure, and reconciliation run on.

Establish and maintain the trading delegation of authority — who may trade what products, instruments, tenors, and sizes, and which approvals are required beyond each authority — keeping it current with roles, strategies, and governance decisions so every trade's authorization has a defined basis.

Construct and maintain the forward price curves the organization values and measures risk with — sourcing market data, building and validating curves by commodity, location, and tenor per approved methodology, and publishing the official curve set on the control calendar.

Coordinate and evidence the daily trading-risk control cycle — performing or obtaining capture-completeness checks, freezing the official market-data set, running or obtaining valuation, position, P&L, and risk-measure outputs, investigating material exceptions, and obtaining the designated control approvals for the daily controlled result.

Coordinate and evidence the month-end trading-risk control cycle — reconciling and reviewing the month's daily controlled results, producing month-end economic valuation, position, P&L, and risk outputs, resolving or formally carrying forward approved exceptions — and provide the controlled economic inputs required by Accounting's reconciliation and close processes.

Establish, maintain, publish, and adjust market-risk limits — by book, strategy, commodity, tenor, and measure — derived from approved risk appetite; administer documented temporary-excess and exception decisions under delegated authority; and tighten or suspend limits when conditions or policy triggers require it.

Compute the organization's market-risk measures — value-at-risk, sensitivities, position and tenor exposures, and the other measures the approved framework requires — from validated positions, curves, and volatilities, publishing them on the control calendar so limits, monitoring, and reporting run on one measured picture.

Continuously watch market risk against limits — detecting breaches and near-breaches, escalating them per policy, tracking them to resolution, and watching concentration and regime signals — so no excursion goes unseen or unescalated.

Produce and analyze the official, controlled position and realized and unrealized P&L picture — explaining daily P&L by its drivers (price, position, new deals, amendments, and other effects), investigating unexplained amounts, and delivering the validated P&L that management, risk, and the accounting reconciliation consume.
Actualizations is performed by scheduler who assigns the final ticket volumes to the trades according to the preset priority.

Update trading deal, movement, and entitlement records with contractually applicable actual quantities, qualities, dates, statuses, and charge determinants from execution, custody-transfer, registry, and other agreed evidence, replacing planned or estimated values so settlement, economic P&L, risk, and downstream reporting use controlled actuals.

Actualize pipeline movements of crude, feedstocks, and products — recording actual receipt and delivery volumes, qualities, and dates from pipeline meter tickets, carrier statements, and shipper reports, applying pipeline loss allowance, quality-bank, proration, or other carrier and tariff adjustments where applicable, and reconciling actuals against nominated and scheduled volumes — so pipeline transactions settle on verified actuals.

Actualize truck movements of crude, feedstocks, and products — recording actual loaded and delivered volumes, qualities, and dates from bills of lading, terminal lifting records, and truck tickets, recorded on the contractually applicable measurement and temperature/volume basis — so truck transactions settle on verified actuals.

Actualize railcar movements of crude, feedstocks, and products — recording actual loaded and received quantities, weights, qualities, and dates from railcar shipping documents, scale weights, and gauging records on the contractually applicable basis — so rail transactions settle on verified actuals.

Actualize marine movements by vessel and barge — recording actual loaded and outturn quantities, qualities, and dates from bills of lading, independent inspection reports, and ship and shore figures per marine measurement practice, and identifying apparent voyage gains, losses, and quantity differences according to the contractual measurement basis — so marine transactions settle on verified actuals.

Actualize terminal and storage transactions — recording transaction-level receipt, delivery, throughput, and contractually relevant storage-balance actuals for the associated deal or capacity arrangement from terminal operator statements, tank gauging records, and throughput reports, and recording verified throughput, storage, blending, and handling charge determinants and applicable contractual bases — so terminal and storage transactions settle on verified actuals.

Actualize crude and condensate lease purchases — recording actual volumes, gravities, and qualities from run tickets and LACT meter records taken at lease-tank custody transfer, applying the contractual gravity, quality, and deduction adjustments and division-of-interest references — so first-purchase transactions settle on verified actuals.

Update environmental-attribute and renewable-instrument trading records from authoritative registry lifecycle events — including issuance or generation, separation where applicable, transfer, acquisition, sale, retirement, and cancellation — and reconcile internal instrument positions to the applicable registry or regulatory system of record.

Manage disputes over what was physically delivered, received, measured, or performed — logging and classifying quantity, quality, and measurement discrepancies, investigating against custody-transfer evidence and independent inspection, coordinating investigation, evidence exchange, and agreement or adjudication of corrected actuals with the relevant external parties under the governing agreement and applicable measurement hierarchy, and closing disputes through corrected actualized records.

Settlements and Accounting process covers deal attributes and deal terms at time of trade execution with counterparty through netting, invoicing and settlement post trade expiry and various accounting postings throughout deal lifecycle.

Determine and complete the financial settlement of trading transactions — calculating amounts owed and due from actualized quantities, contractual prices, and verified charge determinants; generating and validating invoices; netting where agreements provide; preparing, validating, and submitting authorized settlement instructions or payment requests to the designated Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, Treasury, banking, or shared-services process; tracking payment or receipt status; and retaining settlement evidence — so every transaction closes financially on verified actuals and contractual terms.

Settle physical crude oil and condensate purchases and sales — applying contractual pricing, including provisional pricing, deferred pricing, or subsequent price determination where the contract provides, and contractually defined quality adjustments to actualized volumes, issuing and validating invoices, netting where agreements allow, and submitting authorized payment and receipt instructions — so crude transactions complete financially on verified actuals.

Settle natural gas purchases, sales, transportation, and storage — applying index and contract pricing to scheduled and flowing-gas quantities, validating pipeline and counterparty invoices per the applicable business-practice standards, settling imbalances and cash-outs per tariff and contract, and submitting authorized payment and receipt instructions — so gas transactions complete financially on verified quantities.

Settle bilateral financial over-the-counter derivatives — determining settlement amounts from contractual fixings and floating-price observations per the confirmed terms, exchanging and validating settlement calculations with counterparties, netting payments under the governing master agreements, and submitting authorized payment and receipt instructions — so financial trades complete per their documented terms.

Settle pipeline transportation charges with carriers — validating pipeline invoices for tariff transportation, fuel, loss allowance, and related charges against actualized pipeline movements and verified tariff determinants, resolving variances, and submitting authorized payment instructions — so pipeline services complete financially on verified movement actuals.

Settle rail transportation charges with railroads and rail service providers — validating freight and accessorial invoices against actualized rail movements and verified charge determinants, applying contracted and tariff rates, resolving variances, and submitting authorized payment instructions — so rail services complete financially on verified movement actuals.

Settle terminal and storage service charges — validating operator invoices for throughput, storage, blending, handling, and ancillary services against actualized terminal transactions and verified charge determinants and contractual bases, resolving variances, and submitting authorized payment instructions — so terminal and storage services complete financially on verified actuals.

Settle bilateral power transactions outside ISO markets — applying contract and index pricing to scheduled and delivered quantities, validating counterparty invoices and settlement data, netting where agreements provide, and submitting authorized payment and receipt instructions — so bilateral power transactions complete financially on verified quantities.

Settle broker and clearing-member account activity — reconciling broker statements against internal trade, position, and margin records, validating commissions, fees, and charges, preparing, submitting, tracking, and reconciling authorized broker-facing payment or collateral-transfer instructions, including margin transfers, through the designated Treasury, banking, or payment-operations process, and resolving statement discrepancies — so broker accounts remain accurate, funded, and evidenced.

Manage disputes over what is owed, invoiced, received, paid, netted, or applied — logging and classifying settlement discrepancies, investigating against actualized records, contractual terms, and settlement calculations, coordinating resolution with counterparties, carriers, brokers, and operators under the governing agreements, escalating aging or material disputes, and closing them through corrected settlements and evidenced adjustments.

Settle purchases and sales of refinery intermediates and blend components — applying contractual and index-based pricing to actualized volumes and qualities, generating and validating invoices, netting where agreements provide, and submitting authorized payment and receipt instructions — so intermediate transactions complete financially on verified actuals.

Settle purchases and sales of other commodities traded by the organization — such as NGLs, petrochemicals, sulfur, petroleum coke, and other by-products or ancillary commodities — applying contractual pricing to actualized quantities, generating and validating invoices, and submitting authorized payment and receipt instructions on the same settlement discipline as the named commodity processes.

Settle physical refined product purchases and sales — applying contractual and index-based pricing to actualized volumes on the contractual measurement basis, generating and validating invoices, netting where agreements provide, and submitting authorized payment and receipt instructions — so product transactions complete financially on verified actuals.

Settle exchange-traded and cleared transactions — validating and allocating daily settlement variation and final settlement amounts to trades and positions against exchange and clearinghouse values, settling expiries, exercises, and deliveries per contract specifications, and reconciling trade-level settlement outcomes — so cleared positions complete financially per exchange rules.

Settle truck transportation charges with carriers — validating freight invoices against actualized movements and verified freight-charge determinants, applying contracted rates and accessorials, resolving invoice variances, and submitting authorized payment instructions — so trucking services complete financially on verified movement actuals.

Settle marine transportation charges — validating freight, charter hire, and voyage-related invoices against actualized voyages and verified freight, laytime, and voyage-cost determinants, applying charter party and freight-agreement terms, resolving variances, and submitting authorized payment instructions — so marine services complete financially on verified voyage actuals.

Settle crude and condensate first-purchase transactions — calculating amounts due from actualized lease runs under contractual pricing, gravity and quality adjustments, and deductions, producing settlement statements consistent with the division-of-interest references, and submitting authorized payment instructions — so lease purchases complete financially on verified run actuals.

Settle transactions with independent system operators, regional transmission organizations, and power pools — validating ISO settlement statements across the day-ahead and real-time settlement cycles and their subsequent true-up versions, performing independent shadow-settlement checks, disputing discrepancies within ISO timelines, and submitting authorized payment and receipt instructions — so ISO-cleared activity completes financially per market rules.

Settle environmental and renewable instrument transactions — RINs, allowances, RECs, and similar program instruments — calculating amounts due from actualized registry transfers and contractual pricing, generating and validating invoices, and submitting authorized payment instructions against confirmed instrument delivery — so instrument trades complete financially on verified registry actuals.

Manage the controlled working and evidentiary document set used by trading settlement — generating, receiving, validating, distributing, and retaining settlement statements, payment instructions, supporting actualization evidence, and applicable invoices — so every settlement is executed and evidenced from controlled, complete documents.

The capability to record, value, reconcile, and report the financial effects of supply and trading activity by maintaining controlled sub-ledger and general-ledger records; booking authorized settlement outcomes, receivables, payables, actuals, accruals, taxes, and interest obligations; reconciling economic P&L to accounting P&L; and producing controlled financial evidence and reporting within the enterprise accounting-policy framework.

Assess, document, and apply the accounting treatment of trading transactions under approved enterprise policy — derivative versus normal purchase/normal sale scope, own-use, lease, storage, and exchange treatments, and gross-versus-net presentation — obtaining Finance/controller approval or escalation for material, new, complex, or policy-sensitive conclusions, so transactions are recorded under the correct, evidenced treatment.

Calculate, post, and true up accruals for trading activity — un-invoiced delivered or received volumes, expected fees and charges, and estimated prices pending final determination — per the enterprise accrual methodology, so each period's books are complete for activity not yet settled.

Execute transaction- and commodity-tax accounting for supply and trading activity by applying approved tax rules and tax-determination data to transactions, recording tax amounts, maintaining required transaction-level evidence, and preparing controlled tax-accounting and filing-support outputs for the accountable enterprise Tax function.

Develop, maintain, version, and communicate trading-specific accounting procedures, close instructions, and implementation guidance that operationalize Finance-owned enterprise accounting policy for supply and trading activity.
names: Maintain Trading Accounting Procedures and Guidance

terms.definition: Maintain the financial accounting of production and inventory for supply and trading activity — recording and reconciling financial inventory balances and cost-of-sales effects under the enterprise-approved inventory valuation methodology, from verified operational balances — so the financial books carry a complete, correctly valued representation of physical activity.

Execute royalty and interest disbursements arising from first-purchase and marketing arrangements — calculating owner-level distributions from settled lease transactions and division-of-interest references, managing suspense and unclaimed amounts per the applicable requirements, and submitting authorized disbursement instructions — so interest owners are paid correctly and on time.

Record trading receivables, payables, and actuals in the accounting records — recording authorized settlement outcomes and validated invoices in AR/AP, posting actualized transaction values, monitoring open items and aging, and keeping the payables and receivables position complete and current — so the financial position reflects settled and actualized activity.

Maintain the trading sub-ledger as the complete transactional accounting record — ensuring every captured, actualized, and settled transaction posts correctly under its determined treatment, reconciling the sub-ledger to the general ledger, and enforcing period cut-off — so the general ledger can rely on a complete, reconciled trading record.

Reconcile the economic profit and loss produced by the trading risk processes to the profit and loss recorded in the accounting books — identifying, quantifying, explaining, and evidencing expected and unexpected differences by cause — so management, risk, and financial views of trading results are provably consistent.
names: Reconcile Economic PNL to Accounting PNL

terms.definition: Prepare and control the financial documentation and internal financial reporting for supply and trading activity — management reporting on financial results, accounting workpapers and reconciliation evidence, and controlled inputs to external financial reporting through the accountable owners — so financial information about trading is complete, evidenced, and consistently produced.
names: Manage Financial Information Documentation and Reporting

terms.definition: Administer the financial system structures used by trading accounting — chart-of-accounts mapping, ledger and book structures, posting rules and business interface configuration from trading systems to the general ledger, and accounting master data — so postings land correctly, completely, and controllably in the financial records.

Apply cash receipts to open trading receivables — matching bank-reported receipts against invoices, settlement statements, and netting arrangements, investigating and coordinating resolution of unapplied, unidentified, short, and over payments, and evidencing application — so the receivables position is accurate and cash is accounted for daily.

The capability to keep supply and trading activity compliant with external law, regulation, and market rules and with the organization's own compliance framework — maintaining the trading compliance program's policies and procedures, monitoring external regulatory compliance, internal policy adherence, and the operation of compliance-supporting controls, assuring tax compliance, coordinating regulatory reporting obligations with their accountable owners, and managing compliance exceptions through to closure.

Develop and maintain the trading compliance program's policies and procedures — market-conduct rules, information barriers, personal-account dealing, communications and conflicts requirements, regulatory-change management, and compliance monitoring and escalation procedures — within the enterprise compliance and legal governance framework, so trading activity operates under current, communicated compliance requirements.

Monitor supply and trading activity for compliance with external law, regulation, and market rules — market-conduct and anti-manipulation surveillance, position-limit monitoring, exchange and market-rule adherence, licensing and registration status, and completion of regulatory reporting obligations by their owners — surfacing potential violations for assessment and escalation.

Monitor adherence to the organization's internal trading compliance policies — conduct rules, information barriers, personal-account dealing, gifts and entertainment, communications requirements, and required compliance training — surfacing violations and adverse patterns for assessment and escalation.

Monitor the operation of internally implemented controls that support the organization's external trading obligations — verifying that required deal approvals are evidenced, regulatory reporting controls are complete and functioning, surveillance and recordkeeping controls operate as designed, and audit evidence exists — surfacing control failures and gaps to the accountable owners.

Monitor and assure compliance with transaction- and commodity-tax obligations affecting supply and trading activity by reviewing evidence of registration, licensing, exemption-certificate, filing-calendar, and tax-determination-control compliance; coordinating relevant tax-authority notices and examinations with the enterprise Tax function; and escalating material gaps.

Coordinate the trading organization's Renewable Fuel Standard reporting obligations — assembling and quality-assuring RIN transaction, position, and renewable-volume-obligation data from the trading systems and registries, reconciling it to EMTS, and preparing controlled reporting inputs and supporting evidence for the accountable filer — so RFS reports attributable to trading activity are complete, accurate, and evidenced.

Manage compliance exceptions through their lifecycle — logging and classifying identified violations, control failures, and approved deviations, assessing severity and regulatory implications, coordinating waiver, remediation-plan, and closure approvals under the documented compliance delegation, tracking remediation to closure, and evidencing the record — so every compliance gap is visibly owned, decided, and closed.

Govern the environmental compliance credits a company generates, buys, holds and uses, and the clean-fuel tax credits it earns and claims, under one set of controls: provenance, eligibility evidence, valuation, reconciliation and audit.
names: Manage Environmental Credits and Clean-Fuel Incentives

terms.definition: Run the lifecycle of compliance credits for each program: determine the obligation (a Renewable Volume Obligation under the RFS; deficits under LCFS), generate credits from qualifying fuel, buy and sell credits with integrity checks on the counterparty and the credit (MPC runs a RIN integrity program to vet the RINs it buys, MPC FY2025 Form 10-K, Item 1), transfer them between accounts, and retire them to show compliance.

Run the lifecycle of the Section 45Z clean fuel production credit: register as a producer of clean fuel before production (Form 637), document that each fuel qualifies (qualified facility, qualified sale, emissions factor, and from 2026 feedstock from the United States, Mexico or Canada), determine the credit for the taxable year, and claim it with the income tax return (Form 7218).

Manage outbound and inbound claims for demurrage, despatch, detention, and other contractually defined delay or capacity-usage compensation by evaluating verified time, notice, and event evidence under the governing agreement; establishing entitlement or liability; creating, assessing, negotiating, documenting, invoicing, and tracking agreed claims; and escalating unresolved matters through the applicable commercial and legal processes.

Screen completed voyages and terminal operations for potential demurrage, despatch, and detention entitlements and exposures — comparing used against allowed laytime from actualized notices, statements of fact, and timesheets under the governing terms, computing preliminary claim values in both directions, and identifying the contractual deadlines and evidence needed to preserve or defend each claim — so every potential claim is identified before rights lapse.

Build outbound demurrage, despatch, and detention claims — performing the definitive laytime calculation under the governing terms, assembling the supporting evidence (notices of readiness, statements of fact, timesheets, port and terminal logs), verifying contractual notice, documentation, and time-limit requirements are met, obtaining the designated internal review, and issuing the claim to the responsible party — so outbound claims are complete, timely, and defensible.

Register inbound demurrage, despatch, and detention claims — logging received claims, acknowledging where the governing terms require, recording receipt-stage time-limit and documentation observations, and routing claims to assessment — so inbound claims enter a controlled process with their receipt-stage observations captured.

Assess the merit and quantum of inbound claims — recalculating laytime independently from the organization's own actualized records under the governing terms, applying contractual exceptions, interruptions, allocation provisions, notices, and responsibility rules as the governing agreement provides, and determining an evidenced accept, counter, or reject position — so inbound claims are paid only to the extent actually owed.

Pursue issued outbound claims to resolution — presenting the claim and its evidence, responding to counterarguments and counter-calculations, negotiating commercial resolution within delegated claim-settlement authority, obtaining additional approval where a proposed compromise, waiver, credit, set-off, or write-down exceeds that authority, and agreeing resolution or escalating unresolved claims — so outbound entitlements convert to agreed, collectible amounts.

Resolve inbound claims from the assessed position — communicating the assessed position with its evidence, negotiating, accepting, partially accepting, countering, or rejecting the claim within delegated authority, routing concessions, waivers, or formal settlement agreements through the required approval path, and agreeing resolution or escalating unresolved claims — so inbound exposure closes at the evidenced amount, not the claimed one.

Invoice agreed outbound claims — issuing the claim invoice and settlement statement for the negotiated amount with its supporting calculation, submitting the receivable into the designated finance processes, tracking expected receipt, and obtaining confirmation from Accounting that the receivable is booked and cash applied — so agreed entitlements are collected and evidenced.

Process invoices for agreed inbound claims — validating the received invoice against the negotiated resolution and its evidence, preparing and submitting a payment request supported by the agreed resolution and required approvals to the designated Accounts Payable/Treasury process, and evidencing closure — so the organization pays exactly what was agreed, once, with a complete trail.
names: Process Invoice for Agreed Inbound Claim

terms.definition: Crude/feed supply chain management consists of processes required to plan, organize, coordinate & control crude/feed supply & processing at the refinery. This includes crude/feed transportation, slate, and supply & demand management.

The capability to keep feedstock selection running on trustworthy quality and economic information — maintaining validated crude and feedstock quality data, reviewing the integrity of the evaluation models that consume it, and developing the quality-screened term and spot procurement slates that feed the feedstock recommendation and trading execution.

Steward the crude and feedstock quality data used in evaluation, planning, and trading — maintaining current, validated assays and quality records, tracking assay age and representativeness, incorporating new laboratory and cargo data under controlled update procedures, and distributing consistent quality data to the consuming models and processes.

Review whether the feedstock data, yield representations, operating constraints, capacities, market assumptions, and other decision inputs used by feedstock-evaluation and planning models remain current, complete, internally consistent, and representative of the refinery and market conditions; document findings and escalate required corrections to accountable data and model owners.

Develop the recommended term feedstock procurement slate — the portfolio of crudes and feedstocks proposed for supply under agreements with multi-period or continuing commercial commitments, screened for refinery quality compatibility and evaluated for sustained economic attractiveness — so term procurement and the feedstock recommendation rest on a quality-assured base-load supply plan.

Develop the recommended spot feedstock procurement slate — the quality-screened spot supply candidates that address residual demand, supply disruption, quality constraints, timing needs, or economic opportunities after considering committed term supply, ranked by current economic attractiveness and availability — so spot procurement decisions start from a vetted, refinery-compatible option set.

Collect and keep, for each renewable feedstock lot, the evidence its credits depend on: supplier certifications, source location, feedstock type and quantity, and the carbon-intensity data of the pathway it supports, and check it before the lot is used.
names: Manage Renewable Feedstock Traceability and Carbon-Intensity Evidence

terms.definition: Translate the refinery production plan into feedstock supply action — developing the feedstock demand signal, recommending the economically attractive feedstock slate and run rate to Refinery Planning and Optimization, and coordinating the resulting requirements with the trading processes — so feedstock supply is planned against a validated demand and an economically informed recommendation.

Coordinate feedstock supply requirements with the trading processes — translating demand, slate recommendations, and schedule imbalances into requested purchases, sales, or exchanges with their grade, quality, quantity, timing, and delivery requirements, evaluating proposed trades for plan and schedule fit, and incorporating agreed volumes back into the supply plan.

Develop the projected feedstock requirement — quantity, grade, quality, and timing — from the refinery production plan and current inventory and supply positions, maintaining it as plans and positions change, so procurement, slate development, and trading coordination work from one validated demand signal.

Recommend the economically attractive feedstock slate and run rate to Refinery Planning and Optimization — combining the demand signal, procurement slates, market prices, and supply economics into a trading-side recommendation that feeds the binding plan without setting it — so the refinery plan is informed by the best current supply-market view.
names: Plan Optimal Feedstock Slate And Run Rate
Recommend Feedstock Slate And Run Rate

terms.definition: Plan and manage the transportation of purchased crude and feedstocks to the refinery — coordinating movements across pipeline, marine, rail, and truck modes against the supply plan, scheduling deliveries into agreed refinery receipt windows, and planning arrivals with the refinery and terminal operations owners — so purchased feedstock arrives when, where, and how the refinery can receive it.

Coordinate and monitor the commercial and logistical arrangements required to move agreed feedstock volumes under available carrier contracts, capacity rights, nominations, fixtures, and transport agreements — selecting modes and routings, tracking movement status, and resolving in-transit issues with carriers and operators — so every purchased cargo has a managed path to the refinery.

Schedule feedstock deliveries into agreed refinery receipt windows by sequencing confirmed movements against available berth, pipeline-receipt, tankage, quality-segregation, and refinery-receipt constraints, coordinating and confirming proposed receipt windows with the relevant refinery and terminal scheduling and operations owners, and maintaining the delivery schedule as movements and refinery conditions change.

Plan individual feedstock arrivals — coordinating laycans, arrival timing, and berth and discharge sequencing with the terminal and refinery, recommending or coordinating proposed tank destinations with refinery/terminal operations subject to their operational authority, and adjusting the arrival plan as vessels, pipelines, and refinery conditions develop — so each arrival is prepared for timely, safe, and quality-compatible receipt, subject to operational conditions and the governing agreements.

The capability to keep the feedstock supply position sound — monitoring and controlling feedstock inventory positions against operating requirements, and assessing and managing the price, supply, and working-capital risk those positions carry — so the refinery is supplied without avoidable risk or trapped capital.

Assess the price, supply-availability, disruption, quality, concentration, and working-capital risk associated with feedstock inventory positions; recommend inventory, supply, operational, and hedging mitigations to accountable owners; and submit approved hedging requirements to the authorized trading process so risk is visible, understood, and managed within approved appetite.

Monitor and control actual and projected crude and feedstock inventory positions — identifying operating-limit, availability, quality, location, and balance exceptions against refinery requirements and the supply plan, coordinating timely response, and providing reliable current-position information to planning, trading, and logistics.

Refined product supply chain management consist of processes that are required to maintain an optimal supply network. This covers the generation of the demand forecast, associated customer allocations, the demand & supply balancing process & the execution of terminal replenishment.

Analyze the refined-product supply network's market participation — segmenting customers and markets on supply economics, evaluating market attractiveness for supply-network participation, and assessing cost-to-serve performance — and recommend where and whom the network should serve profitably, informing the network and participation decisions of the accountable commercial and planning owners.

Segment the customers and demand points served by the refined-product supply network on supply-economics dimensions — volume, product mix, location, delivery mode, service requirements, and margin contribution — so participation, service, and cost-to-serve analysis work from an economically meaningful segmentation.

Evaluate market attractiveness for supply-network participation using accessible demand, realizable supply margin, logistics reach and cost, supply reliability, specification and regulatory constraints, and network fit — so participation recommendations rest on a consistent supply-network economic evaluation.

Assess the full cost of serving customers, segments, and markets from the refined-product supply network — supply, storage, handling, primary and secondary logistics, and service costs against realized margins — identifying where the network serves profitably, marginally, or at a loss, so participation and service recommendations rest on evidenced economics.

Manage refined-product demand on the supply side — maintaining the operational demand picture the supply chain runs on, forecasting location-level product demand for supply operations, and managing product-exchange volumes as a balancing lever — so supply operations, replenishment, and trading coordination work from one current, operational demand view.

Manage the operational refined-product demand picture — consolidating current orders, lifting patterns, committed volumes, and forecast demand by product and location, comparing it against available supply, and surfacing imbalances for supply, replenishment, and trading action — so shortfalls and surpluses are visible and acted on before they become failures.

Coordinate operational utilization of product-exchange entitlements to support approved demand and supply requirements by monitoring available exchange positions, planning proposed lifting and delivery use by location and period, and communicating utilization requirements to the relevant agreement, trading, supply, and scheduling processes.

Forecast refined-product demand operationally for the supply-chain context — projecting short-horizon demand by product, location, and period from lifting history, orders, seasonality, and local market signals, calibrated against the published enterprise forecast — so supply operations and replenishment run on location-level demand projections at operational granularity.

Fulfill approved refined-product replenishment and supply requirements from Supply & Trading sources by coordinating product availability at purchased-supply, exchange, transfer, and third-party source points; confirming feasible supply and transport arrangements; and handing approved movements to the processes that schedule, actualize, and settle them.

Coordinate commercial supply status at the source points where Supply And Trading supplies primary distribution — monitoring availability, loading capability, and product quality at purchased-supply, exchange, transfer, and third-party terminal locations, resolving supply issues with operators and counterparties, and keeping source-point status current for replenishment fulfillment and scheduling.

Fulfill network replenishment requirements from Supply And Trading sources — receiving the replenishment quantities and timing decided by the network replenishment owner, sourcing them from purchased, exchanged, and transferred product where own production does not cover them, and confirming fulfillment plans, constraints, and exceptions back — so replenishment decisions are met without S&T re-deciding them.

Coordinate transportation arrangements for Supply And Trading-sourced primary product movements — pipeline, marine, rail, and truck arrangements under available carrier contracts, capacity, and transport agreements for volumes S&T supplies into the network — providing confirmed movement requirements to the processes that own scheduling and actualization.
Product distribution management involves managing product and transportation agreements, terminal operations.

Negotiate, maintain commercial requirements for, and coordinate lifecycle changes to product-side agreements that enable product exchanges, customer delivery commitments, and storage/throughput access, so dependent supply, distribution, and settlement processes operate against current commercially agreed terms.

Negotiate and administer product exchange agreements — the terms under which product is exchanged with other suppliers across locations and time — owning the entitlement rules, differentials, and contractual imbalance calculation and treatment, and recommending or making delegated commercial decisions on imbalance resolution, so exchange supply operates against governed agreements with controlled balances.

Negotiate and administer customer-facing product transport and delivery agreements — the delivery terms linked to product sale and marketing arrangements, including delivered pricing bases, delivery service commitments, and receiving requirements — so product deliveries to customers operate against current, correct commercial delivery terms.

Negotiate storage and throughput agreements — leased tankage, cavern capacity, terminal throughput, and handling arrangements — establishing capacity, fee structures, service levels, and quality-protection terms, obtaining required commercial approvals, coordinating execution through Legal and authorized signatories, and handing executed agreements to the contract record and deal capture, so storage and throughput capacity is secured on sound commercial terms.

The capability to operate and maintain company-managed marketing and distribution terminals, loading facilities, and associated distribution fleet assets where the business unit is the designated operating entity, including site safety execution, fleet capability management, and site-asset integrity and availability.

Operate the safety programs at company-managed terminal and fleet operations — hazardous-materials handling safety, staff safety training and procedures, and contractor safety qualification and control — executing the enterprise EHS framework at site level, so people and operations at company-managed facilities are protected and compliant.

Manage the capacity, readiness, safety, compliance, maintenance, and performance of company-operated and contracted road-delivery fleet resources so Secondary Distribution Management can assign safe, qualified, and available vehicles and carriers to approved delivery schedules.

Manage the operational availability, condition, integrity coordination, and business-use allocation of company-managed marketing and distribution terminal assets — including tanks, racks, meters, additive systems, vapor-recovery equipment, and supporting infrastructure — within enterprise engineering, maintenance, and EHS standards.

Marketing Includes Processes Such As Performing Market Analysis, Developing Marketing Strategy, New Product Development, Managing Retail Marketing Operations. It Includes Processes Required To Take The Products & Services From Strategic Conception, Through Planning To Operational Execution.
Market analysis & insight process determines market attractiveness & identifies evolving opportunities & threats as to the industry in general & company specifically.

Analyze the downstream product markets the company serves or could serve — market size, demand and supply balances, channel structure, margin pools, and regulatory and structural change — through a recurring, governed analysis cycle, so marketing strategy and planning decisions rest on a current, evidenced view of the market.

Source and collect the market data the market-analysis cycle needs — government statistics, licensed market data, industry publications, and internal sales and channel data — qualifying sources, respecting licensing terms, and organizing collected data for analysis.
names: Source & Collect Information for Market Analysis

terms.definition: Define each market-analysis cycle's objectives, questions, scope, and method with the consuming stakeholders — which markets, products, channels, and periods, answering which decisions — so analysis effort lands on the questions strategy and planning actually need answered.
