names: Define Analysis Objectives & Scope for Market Analysis

terms.definition: Analyze the collected market data against the defined objectives — market sizing, demand and supply balance, channel and margin structure, trend and scenario analysis — producing evidenced analytical results with their assumptions and confidence stated.

Document and distribute the market-analysis findings — governed findings records with their evidence, assumptions, and confidence — to the consuming strategy, planning, and insight processes, maintaining the findings library so analysis is reusable and auditable.

Analyze the company's own position and performance in its downstream markets — market share, portfolio and asset position, capability strengths and gaps, and performance against the market, using approved internal data, external benchmarks, and stated comparability assumptions — through a recurring, governed analysis cycle, so strategy is built on an honest view of where the company stands.

Source and collect the data the company-analysis cycle needs — governed internal financial, volume, share, and capability data, and the external benchmarks to compare against — respecting the data owners' controls and organizing the data for analysis.
names: Source & Collect Information for Company Analysis

terms.definition: Define each company-analysis cycle's objectives, questions, scope, and method with the consuming stakeholders — which businesses, markets, capabilities, and periods, answering which strategic questions — so self-analysis lands where strategy needs it.
names: Define Analysis Objectives & Scope for Company Analysis

terms.definition: Analyze the company's position against the defined objectives — share and share-trend analysis, portfolio and asset-position assessment, capability strengths and gaps, and performance versus market and benchmarks — producing evidenced results with assumptions and confidence stated.

Document and distribute the company-analysis findings — governed records with evidence, assumptions, and confidence — to strategy, planning, and Marketing Insight and Metrics Stewardship, maintaining the findings library.

Analyze end-consumer behavior in the company's downstream markets — needs, preferences, buying patterns, journey and experience drivers, and segment dynamics — through a recurring, governed analysis cycle operating within the applicable privacy frameworks, so consumer-facing strategy rests on evidenced consumer understanding.

Source and collect the consumer data the analysis cycle needs — research studies, panels, transaction and loyalty data, and demographic and market data — within consent, privacy, and licensing constraints, and organize it for analysis.
names: Source & Collect Information for Consumer Analysis

terms.definition: Define each consumer-analysis cycle's objectives, questions, scope, and method with the consuming stakeholders — which segments, behaviors, journeys, and markets, answering which proposition and experience questions — so consumer research answers real decisions.
names: Define Analysis Objectives & Scope for Consumer Analysis

terms.definition: Analyze consumer data against the defined objectives — segmentation and segment dynamics, needs and preference analysis, behavior and journey analysis, and experience drivers — producing evidenced results with assumptions and confidence stated, within the privacy constraints the data carries.

Document and distribute consumer-analysis findings — governed records with evidence, assumptions, and confidence, respecting the privacy classification of underlying data — to proposition, experience, and planning consumers and Marketing Insight and Metrics Stewardship, maintaining the findings library.

Analyze the company's direct customers and branded marketers — commercial and industrial customers, resellers, and the branded wholesalers, jobbers, and distributors who market under or alongside the brand — their needs, economics, performance, and relationship health, through a recurring, governed analysis cycle, so B2B and channel strategy rests on evidenced counterparty understanding.

Source and collect customer and marketer data for the analysis cycle — volumes, margins, service and relationship records, marketer network data, and external context — under the applicable data controls, organized for analysis.
names: Source & Collect Information for Customer And Marketer Analysis

terms.definition: Define each customer-and-marketer analysis cycle's objectives, questions, scope, and method with the consuming stakeholders — which segments, channels, marketers, and periods, answering which proposition and channel questions.
names: Define Analysis Objectives & Scope for Customer And Marketer Analysis

terms.definition: Analyze customer and marketer data against the defined objectives — needs and segment analysis, channel and counterparty economics, performance and share-of-wallet, and relationship health — producing evidenced results with assumptions and confidence stated.

Document and distribute customer-and-marketer findings — governed records with evidence, assumptions, and confidence, handled per commercial-sensitivity classification — to proposition, channel, and sales consumers and Marketing Insight and Metrics Stewardship, maintaining the findings library.
names: Document Findings of Customer And Marketer Analysis

terms.definition: Analyze competitors in the company's downstream markets — their positions, conduct, capabilities, network moves, and likely responses — through a recurring, governed analysis cycle using legitimately obtained information, so strategy anticipates the competition it will actually face.

Source and collect competitor information from legitimate sources — public filings and disclosures, licensed market data, observable market conduct, and published network and pricing information — recording provenance, and never through anti-competitive exchange or illegitimate means.
names: Source & Collect Information for Competitor Analysis

terms.definition: Define each competitor-analysis cycle's objectives, questions, scope, and method with the consuming stakeholders — which competitors, markets, and dimensions, answering which strategic and response questions.
names: Define Analysis Objectives & Scope for Competitor Analysis

terms.definition: Analyze competitor information against the defined objectives — position and share assessment, conduct and strategy inference, capability and economics estimation, and likely-response analysis — producing evidenced results that state what is known, inferred, and assumed.

Document and distribute competitor-analysis findings — governed records separating fact, inference, and assumption, handled per sensitivity classification — to strategy, planning, and pricing consumers and Marketing Insight and Metrics Stewardship, maintaining the findings library.

The capability to synthesize governed market, company, consumer, customer/marketer, and competitor findings into decision-ready marketing insight; maintain shared marketing-analysis metrics, definitions, baselines, and evidence lineage; and monitor insight adoption and analytical effectiveness.

Terminal Loading consist of processes such as monitoring customer sales activity and implementing control strategies based upon supply, customer credit and/or contract limitations. Allocation decisions are based on evaluating deals and transaction data to determine which product at the terminal should be made available to the customers. It is responsible for sending locks and unlocks to the terminal when it determines that availability should change.

Set up and maintain authorized customers, carriers, and drivers in terminal loading systems: create lifting-authorization records in the terminal automation system from governed commercial, credit, and master data; assign loading credentials and permitted terminals, products, and supply positions; keep authorizations current as commercial, credit, and tax status change; and deactivate access when eligibility ends.
names: Set Up and Maintain Terminal Customer Authorization
Setup and Maintain Customer In Terminal

terms.definition: Receive and process customer lifting forecasts and nominations at terminals: validate nominated volumes against supply positions, allocations, and terminal capability for the nomination period; confirm, adjust, or decline nominations within approved rules; manage in-cycle revisions; and maintain the confirmed commercial lifting outlook that supply, replenishment, and allocation processes consume.
names: Process Customer Lifting Forecasts and Nominations

terms.definition: Enforce approved allocation controls at terminals and loading racks: translate plan-level allocation decisions and confirmed customer lifting nominations into customer, product, and period lifting limits in terminal loading systems; monitor liftings against limits; apply authorized proration and shortage procedures; and adjust controls as supply positions and confirmed nominations change.

Record concluded terminal sales arrangements — rack and spot sales, branded and unbranded supply arrangements, and terminal-specific pricing arrangements — completely and promptly in the governed commercial system: customer, product, terminal, volume basis, price and price mechanism, duration, and terms references — so authorized deals are available to customer setup, nomination processing, allocation, pricing application, and billing.

Strategy process establishes target markets to work in and, at a micro level, provides the strategy for where store locations should be established. For B2B this considers supply envelopes & establishes target geographic markets.

Develop and maintain the approved brand strategy for the company's downstream fuels and products marketing — brand positioning, brand architecture, and where and how the brand competes — through a recurring, hypothesis-driven strategy cycle grounded in the governed marketing evidence base and the applicable enterprise delegation and approval process, so brand investments and branded-channel commitments follow deliberate, evidenced, approved direction.

Formulate the alternative strategic operating models through which the brand could go to market — branded dealer and marketer networks, company-operated retail, unbranded participation, and mixed models — and evaluate them against the brand objectives and the governed evidence base.
names: Formulate and Evaluate Strategic Operating Alternative
Formulate and Evaluate Strategic Operating Alternatives
Formulate and Evaluate Strategic Operating Alternatives (Brand)

terms.definition: Establish the brand objectives and the testable strategic hypotheses for each brand-strategy cycle — what the brand must achieve, in which markets and channels, and which beliefs about consumers, customers, and competitors the strategy depends on.

Develop the brand hypotheses into testable propositions and test them against evidence — analysis findings, consumer and customer research, pilots and market tests where authorized — so the brand strategy commits only to beliefs that survived contact with evidence.

Develop or update the brand strategy — positioning, brand architecture, branded-channel participation, and investment direction — from the tested hypotheses and evaluated alternatives, secure the applicable approvals, and issue the approved strategy to the design, planning, and execution branches.

Develop and maintain the approved value proposition offered to the company's direct customers and branded marketers — the strategic promise concerning supply, brand, program, service, and support value made to commercial customers, resellers, jobbers, distributors, and dealers — through a recurring, hypothesis-driven strategy cycle, so B2B and channel relationships are built on a deliberate, evidenced, approved promise.

Test the customer-and-marketer value proposition against evidence — counterparty findings, direct customer and marketer feedback, win/loss and retention signals, and competitive benchmarks — so the proposition strategy commits only to a promise the evidence supports.
names: Test Customer and Marketer Value Proposition

terms.definition: Formulate alternative strategic models for delivering the customer-and-marketer value proposition — supply-led, brand-and-program-led, service-led, and mixed models across the channel structure — and evaluate them against the CVP objectives and the governed evidence base.
names: Formulate and Evaluate Customer and Marketer Value Proposition Alternatives
Formulate and Evaluate Strategic Operating Alternatives (CVP)

terms.definition: Establish the principles and objectives of the customer-and-marketer value proposition — what the promise must achieve for the company and for its customers and marketers, and the principles any proposition must satisfy.
names: Establish Customer and Marketer Value Proposition Principles and Objectives

terms.definition: Develop or update the customer-and-marketer value-proposition strategy from the tested elements and evaluated alternatives, secure the applicable approvals, and issue the approved proposition to offer definition, channel strategy, and channel management.
names: Develop and Update Customer and Marketer Value Proposition Strategy

terms.definition: Develop and maintain the approved value proposition offered to end consumers in the company's downstream markets — the strategic promise concerning fuel, convenience, loyalty, and experience value — through a recurring, hypothesis-driven strategy cycle grounded in governed consumer evidence, so consumer-facing offers and experiences deliver a deliberate, approved promise.

Test the consumer value proposition against evidence — governed consumer findings, research, and authorized concept and market tests — so the consumer promise commits only to what the evidence supports.

Formulate alternative strategic models for delivering the consumer value proposition — fuel-led, convenience-led, loyalty-led, digital-led, and mixed models — and evaluate them against the proposition objectives and the governed evidence base.
names: Formulate and Evaluate Consumer Value Proposition Alternatives

terms.definition: Establish the principles and objectives of the consumer value proposition — what the consumer promise must achieve and the principles any candidate proposition must satisfy.
names: Establish Consumer Value Proposition Principles and Objectives

terms.definition: Develop or update the consumer value-proposition strategy from the tested elements and evaluated alternatives, secure the applicable approvals, and issue the approved proposition to offer definition, experience strategy, and consumer-facing planning.
names: Develop and Update Consumer Value Proposition Strategy

terms.definition: Develop and maintain the approved strategic channel-of-trade direction for downstream sales and distribution — which routes to market the company participates in, their strategic roles, and the target channel mix — through a recurring cycle of channel diagnostics and hypothesis-driven strategy development under the applicable enterprise approvals, so channel design and channel management execute a deliberate, evidenced, approved direction.

Diagnose the performance and economics of each channel of trade the company participates in — volumes, margins, cost-to-serve, share, counterparty health, and structural trends — producing the evidenced channel picture the channel strategy is built on.

Establish the channel operating objectives and develop the channel-strategy hypothesis — the proposed channel participation, roles, and target mix with the beliefs it depends on stated testably — for evaluation and approval at the channel-strategy level.
names: Establish Channel Operating Objectives and Channel Strategy Hypothesis
Establish operating Objectives and develop Channel Strategy Hypothesis

terms.definition: Develop and maintain the approved customer-experience strategy for the company's downstream customer and consumer interactions — the experience aspiration, guiding principles, and strategic pillars that every channel, offer, and service interaction is designed against — through a recurring strategy cycle grounded in governed consumer and customer evidence.

Identify the customer-experience aspiration — the target experience the company commits to across its consumer and customer interactions — from the brand strategy, value propositions, and governed experience evidence.

Define the guiding principles that translate the experience aspiration into decision rules — the consistent behaviors, standards of treatment, and design tenets every channel, offer, and service decision must satisfy.

Establish the strategic pillars of the customer-experience strategy — the small set of experience priorities the company will invest in and be known for — with their intended outcomes and the evidence basis for each.

Offer design & development process consist of the elements of the go-to-market approach determined in the marketing operations strategy. It links the long-term strategy with the operational planning by detailing all strategic aspects (customer offer, sales channel & operations, distribution network).

Define the concrete customer offers that deliver the approved value propositions — which customer groups are targeted, what each offer contains, how it is validated, and how its performance will be measured — through a recurring offer-design cycle, so execution sells defined, validated offers rather than improvised ones.
Define the customer groups each offer targets — selecting and prioritizing segments from the governed segmentation evidence — so offers are designed for identified groups rather than everyone.

Define the content of each customer offer — the product, service, program, and experience elements assembled for the target group, with the commercial logic connecting them — implementing the approved value proposition as a concrete, specifiable offer.

Validate defined offers against evidence before release — customer and consumer response, commercial viability, operational deliverability, and consistency with the approved proposition — so offers reach planning and execution already tested.

Define the measurement framework for customer offers — the metric definitions, baselines, targets, and measurement responsibilities by which offer performance will be managed — as evidence-layer measures with governed routing toward enterprise KPIs.

Establish and manage the pricing strategy for downstream marketing — the strategic pricing approach, the integrated pricing strategy and approved price parameters and guardrails across products, channels, and customer groups, and the piloting and performance feedback that keep it evidenced — within the applicable price-related legal frameworks and approvals, so pricing execution operates against governed, deliberate pricing direction.

Define the strategic pricing approach for downstream marketing — the pricing postures (value, cost-plus, index-linked, market-following, premium) by product, channel, and customer group, consistent with the strategic role of price set by the strategy branch.

Develop the integrated pricing strategy — the approved price architecture, differential logic, index-linkage principles, corridors and guardrails, and pricing rules that connect postures across products, channels, and customer groups into one coherent, legally defensible system — issued as governed direction to the pricing execution processes.

Analyze the performance of deployed pricing — realization against architecture, margin and volume effects, competitive position, and rule adherence — producing the recurring evidence that keeps the pricing strategy honest.

Conduct authorized pricing pilots — controlled, time-bounded tests of pricing changes in defined markets or channels — measuring effects before strategy-wide deployment, within the same legal guardrails as deployed pricing.

Define the measurement framework for pricing — realization, margin, differential-integrity, and competitive-position measures with their definitions, baselines, targets, and measurement responsibilities — as evidence-layer measures with governed routing toward enterprise KPIs.

Design the sales and distribution channel system that implements the approved channel strategy — segmenting channels, defining the channel portfolio, creating channel-specific offerings, and developing channel structure, size, and engagement models — so channel management executes a designed system rather than an accumulation of arrangements.

Create the channel-specific offerings and value propositions — what each channel of trade receives from the company and offers onward — implementing the approved customer, marketer, and consumer propositions in each channel's terms.

Define the channel portfolio — which channel segments the company serves through which channel types, with what portfolio balance — implementing the approved channel participation and target mix as a designed portfolio.

Segment the channel landscape for design purposes — grouping channels and channel participants by role, economics, capability, and service needs — producing the segmentation the portfolio and engagement models are designed against.

Develop the structure, size, and engagement model for each channel segment — coverage and capacity, roles and responsibilities between company and channel, and the engagement cadence and support model — completing the designed channel system.
names: Develop Channel Structure, Size & Engagement Model

terms.definition: Define the measurement framework for the channel system — coverage, throughput, economics, and engagement measures with their definitions, baselines, targets, and measurement responsibilities — as evidence-layer measures with governed routing toward enterprise KPIs.

Develop and maintain the approved retail-network design—operating-model alternatives, target footprint, outlet formats, market coverage, and location criteria—within approved channel strategy and investment constraints, so site investment and network-development processes act against an evidence-based network blueprint.

Define the target locations for the retail network — trade-area criteria, location profiles, and prioritized location targets — from consumer, market, and network evidence, producing the location targets the investment and real-estate processes execute against.

Formulate the strategic operating alternatives for the retail network — company-operated, dealer-operated, and mixed network models within the approved channel mix — and evaluate them against network objectives, economics, and constraints.
names: Formulate And Evaluate Strategic Operating Alternatives (network Strategy)
Formulate and Evaluate Strategic Operating Alternatives (Network)

terms.definition: Define the target size of the retail network — outlet counts or ranges, formats, and coverage by market and segment — consistent with the chosen network model, the approved channel mix, and validated capacity and economics.

Define the measurement framework for the retail network — coverage, throughput, unit economics, and network-health measures with their definitions, baselines, targets, and measurement responsibilities — as evidence-layer measures with governed routing toward enterprise KPIs.

Define the marketing communications strategy that carries the approved brand and value propositions to their audiences — integrating the media, direct, advertising, point-of-sale, digital, and internal communication strategies into one coherent direction — within advertising and marketing law, so communications planning and execution deliver one coherent, lawful voice.

Define the media strategy — which paid, owned, and earned media channels carry the communications strategy, with what roles, weights, and principles — so media planning buys against deliberate strategic direction.

Define the direct marketing strategy — how the company contacts identified customers and prospects one-to-one across mail, email, phone, and messaging — within consent, privacy, and marketing-communication law, so direct outreach is deliberate, targeted, and lawful.

Define the advertising strategy — the strategic role, audiences, claims territory, and creative principles of paid advertising — within truth-in-advertising and substantiation requirements, so advertising builds the brand on claims the company can prove.

Define the point-of-sale communication strategy — how the brand and offers are communicated at forecourts, stores, and other points of sale — coordinating brand, offer, and pricing communication where the customer actually decides.

Define the digital marketing strategy — the strategic role of digital channels, platforms, and data-driven techniques across the communications mix — within privacy and online-advertising requirements, so digital investment follows deliberate direction rather than platform momentum.

Developing a program to promote the objectives, values, products and services of the company to its employees by treating them as potential customers, in order to extend company client base, increase employee engagement or to foster brand advocacy.

Define the measurement framework for marketing communications — reach, engagement, effectiveness, and efficiency measures across the communication channels with their definitions, baselines, targets, and measurement responsibilities — as evidence-layer measures with governed routing toward enterprise KPIs.

Design the blueprint for how Marketing operates approved strategies and designs, including business-process architecture, role/capability requirements, organizational interfaces, procedural frameworks, control points, and measurement requirements, without setting headcount, appointing individuals, owning enterprise policy, or implementing technology architecture.

Develop the business process blueprint for the marketing operating model — the end-to-end processes, handoffs, and control points through which the marketing strategies and designs operate — at blueprint level, for the operating processes to implement.

Develop the organizational blueprint for the marketing operating model — the capabilities, roles, and organizational constructs the process blueprint requires — at blueprint level, without setting headcount or making appointments.

Translate the approved channel-of-trade mix and channel-design outputs into the capabilities, processes, service models, role types, control requirements, technology needs, and organizational interfaces required to operate each channel — without deciding, revising, approving, or reopening the channel mix.
names: Translate Channel-of-Trade Mix into Operating Model Requirements

terms.definition: Define the procedural frameworks and guidelines under which the marketing operating model runs — the standard procedures, working guidelines, and escalation paths that implement enterprise policies in marketing's operations — within, never in place of, the policies owned by their accountable functions.

Define the measurement framework for the marketing operating model — process performance, capability health, and operating-efficiency measures with their definitions, baselines, targets, and measurement responsibilities — as evidence-layer measures with governed routing toward enterprise KPIs.

New product & service development process details step-by-step procedure to do feasibility study for a new product and conceptualize it, defines vision based on market need and developed implementation plan, and manages R&D collaboration, licensing & IP, and lifecycle management.

Set the innovation vision and implementation plans for downstream products and services — where the company will innovate, which market needs and signals justify it, and how R&D effort will be mobilized — through a recurring visioning cycle grounded in the governed evidence base, so concept and development work runs against deliberate innovation direction.

Identify the market needs the innovation program should serve — unmet and emerging customer, consumer, and channel needs read from the governed evidence base on the innovation-opportunity lens — prioritized as innovation opportunities with their evidence.

Continuously sense the market, technology, regulatory, and competitive signals relevant to downstream product and service innovation — a standing scan that feeds needs identification and planning with early, sourced, reliability-rated signals.

Develop the R&D implementation plans that mobilize the innovation vision — programs, priorities, capability and partner needs, and resource requirements — as approval-ready recommendations into the applicable delegated authorities.

Develop and evaluate product and service concepts — ideation from evidenced needs, research on candidate concepts, and feasibility assessment across market, technical, commercial, and regulatory dimensions — so only concepts that survive evidence and feasibility reach development.

Generate and shape product and service ideas from the prioritized needs, sensing signals, and collaboration inputs — a managed idea pipeline with capture, enrichment, and screening — feeding candidate concepts to research and feasibility.

Conduct the research that tests candidate concepts — customer and consumer concept research, technical investigation, and market and commercial assessment — producing feasibility evidence with stated confidence for the concept recommendation.

Manage the concept-research activity — commissioning, standards, quality, and completion of the studies the concept lifecycle runs — so research is governed, comparable, and compliant without this process performing the research itself.

Develop new and improved downstream products and services from approved concepts — governed development programs, per-product development execution, and controlled product and service change — within the applicable regulatory and quality gates, so what reaches offers and launch is developed, compliant, and controlled.

Coordinate the product and service development program — evidence-based stage-gate reviews, development standards, cross-functional coordination, and program-level tracking — recording gate outcomes under the applicable delegation of authority.

Conduct the development of each product or service — specification, formulation or service design, testing and validation, and pre-launch readiness evidence — from gate entry to development completion under the program's standards.

Manage controlled change to existing products and services by assessing specification, formulation, service-design, regulatory, quality, supply, customer, pricing, tax, data, offer, channel, inventory, and operational impacts; obtaining required approvals; and coordinating effective-dated implementation and transition.

The capability to manage the company's intellectual assets and licensing on the business side — maintaining the intellectual-asset framework, coordinating registration, valuing assets for decisions, protecting assets operationally, exploiting them commercially, and stewarding the asset portfolio — with all IP legal work executed by Legal & Corporate Communications.

Establish and maintain the intellectual-asset framework — asset categories, identification and disclosure procedures, ownership and decision-rights principles, and handling rules — operationalizing approved Legal IP policy, so intellectual assets are recognized and handled consistently from creation.

Coordinate the registration of registrable intellectual property — identifying registrable assets, preparing business input, and developing business recommendations for Legal-executed filings and maintenance — never filing, prosecuting, or making legal determinations itself.

Assess the commercial value of intellectual assets — their contribution, market relevance, and licensing potential — as decision evidence for protection, exploitation, and portfolio choices, without owning financial valuation policy.

Protect intellectual assets operationally — confidentiality and trade-secret practice, misuse monitoring, and coordination of enforcement through Legal — continuously, across everything the framework classifies as worth protecting.

Exploit intellectual assets commercially — licensing out, brand and technology licensing arrangements, and contribution to products and partnerships — negotiating business terms within delegated authority while Legal drafts and executes every agreement.

Steward the intellectual-asset portfolio — the maintained inventory of assets and registrations, their cost and value balance, and recommendations to maintain, renew, license, or prune — coordinated through Legal for every registration action.

Manage the lifecycle and portfolio of downstream products, services, and R&D initiatives by identifying technology needs, valuing and assessing portfolio elements, and developing evidence-based stage, stop, accelerate, extend, reposition, and retirement recommendations for the applicable delegated authorities.

Identify the technology needs and opportunities the product and R&D portfolios imply — capability gaps, emerging technologies worth evaluating, and renewal needs — feeding portfolio valuation and R&D planning.

Value R&D projects and the product and service portfolios for prioritization — commercial value, strategic fit, risk, resource demand, and option value with stated assumptions and confidence — as decision evidence, not financial accounting.

Assess the product, service, and R&D portfolios against strategy — composition, balance, readiness, performance, and lifecycle position — producing the evidenced portfolio picture the recommendation step works from.

Develop the portfolio recommendations and track delegated decisions — consolidating assessments into stage, stop, accelerate, extend, reposition, and retirement recommendations across the product, service, and R&D portfolios, submitting them to the applicable delegated authorities, and tracking execution of approved decisions through the accountable processes.
names: Develop Portfolio Recommendations and Track Decisions
Manage Product, Service, and R&D Portfolios

terms.definition: Coordinate the collaboration channels through which product and service innovation works with manufacturing, customers and technical service, research partners, and marketing — consistent intake, IP, and confidentiality controls across all channels — so collaboration accelerates innovation without leaking assets or blurring operational boundaries.

Collaborate with refining, blending, and manufacturing on product innovation — developability, blend and formulation feasibility, scale-up, and trial production — informing development without directing any manufacturing operation.

Collaborate with customers and technical service on product innovation — performance needs, field experience, and field trials — under the applicable privacy, confidentiality, and intake controls, feeding real-use evidence into concepts and development.

Collaborate with external research partners — universities, institutes, suppliers, and technology providers — on research and development of mutual interest, under agreements Legal executes and the IP framework governs.

Collaborate with the marketing strategy, design, and planning functions on product and service innovation — carrying market-facing requirements into R&D and innovation results back into offers, communications, and launch preparation.

Marketing sales & operations planning consist of processes that define the go-to-market approach to a level of detail that enables activity planning, forecasting, & performance review against each of the elements (customer offer, sales channel & operations, distribution network).

Plan the sales effort that delivers the approved strategies — the agreed sales-input process into the governed demand forecast, allocated sales targets, account plans, and the margin-gap feedback loop — so sales execution runs against deliberate, evidenced plans rather than improvised quotas.

Determine and allocate sales targets — volume, margin, and mix commitments by segment, channel, account group, and period — from approved plans and the governed forecast, as managerial commitments under the applicable approvals, never as a substitute forecast.

Develop and agree the sales-side input process into the governed demand forecast — which sales intelligence, account plans, and pipeline evidence feed Produce Demand Forecast, in what form, cadence, and quality — never producing or adjusting the forecast itself.

Perform account planning for the accounts and account groups the sales plan prioritizes — objectives, opportunity maps, action plans, and resource assumptions per account — feeding execution and the forecast-input process with account-level evidence.

Analyze the gaps between the demand forecast, sales plan, targets, and actual margin performance — where assumptions, plans, and commitments diverged from governed actuals, and why — producing the evidence the next planning cycle corrects from.
names: Analyze Gaps Between Forecast & Actual Margins
Analyze Gaps Between Forecast, Plan, Targets, and Actual Margin Performance

terms.definition: Integrate the advertising and media plans across campaigns, brands, and channels into one coherent plan — a single calendar, budget envelope, and priority set implementing the approved media and advertising strategies — so buying and execution work from one integrated plan rather than competing campaign plans.

Plan the marketing communications that deliver the approved communications strategy — from needs and target groups through mix models, budgets, and campaign development to the preparation and controlled release of communications deliverables — handing in-channel program execution to Marketing Plan Execution.
Identify the marketing communications needs each planning cycle must serve — which offers, propositions, launches, and channel priorities need communications support, with what urgency and evidence.

Coordinate production, approval readiness, controlled release, and handoff of brand advertising and communications deliverables — brand-building campaign materials from approved packages to execution — recording readiness while the accountable approvers authorize release.
names: Prepare and Release Brand Advertising and Communications Deliverables

terms.definition: Identify the target groups each communications need addresses — selecting audiences from the governed segmentation and targeting evidence within the privacy, fairness, and contactability controls.

Develop and update the marketing mix model — how communications effort and spend distribute across channels, campaigns, and audiences for best effect — using performance evidence and the strategy's channel roles.
names: Develop and Update Marketing Mix Model

terms.definition: Develop and update campaigns — objectives, audiences, messages, channel plans, creative briefs, and measurement hooks per campaign — within the communications plan and the claims and brand controls, assembled as approval-routed campaign packages.

Define the communications resource allocation and budgets — distributing the approved envelope across needs, campaigns, and channels per the mix model — as allocations under the applicable delegation of authority.

Define the communications plan — the consolidated plan of campaigns, channels, audiences, timings, budgets, and responsibilities for the cycle — the single planning artifact the release preparation and execution work from.

Manage the use of the brand in communications — a planning and material-review control applying the standards owned by Brand Standards Management within planned communications materials, release packages, and placements — escalating deviations to the accountable owners.

Coordinate production, approval readiness, controlled release, and handoff of promotional advertising deliverables — from approved campaign packages to execution — recording readiness while the accountable approvers authorize release.
names: Prepare and Release Promotional Advertising Deliverables

terms.definition: Coordinate production, approval readiness, controlled release, and handoff of internal marketing communications — the campaigns and materials that promote the company's products, objectives, and marketing programs to employees — within the internal-communications boundary shared with Corporate Communications and HR.
names: Prepare and Release Internal Marketing Communications

terms.definition: Plan the promotions program — the promotional plan and the event, point-of-purchase, and site-level marketing calendars — within the pricing, claims, and POS boundaries and the conditional readiness framework, so promotion execution runs from one governed promotional calendar set.
Define the promotional plan — which promotions run, for which offers, audiences, channels, and periods, with what mechanics, budgets, and success measures — within the pricing and claims guardrails.

Create and maintain the promotional event calendar — the scheduled promotional events across channels and periods — synchronized with the communications plan, supply and inventory readiness, and the forecast-input process.

Create and maintain the point-of-purchase promotional calendar — the scheduled POP promotional activity at forecourts, stores, and other points of sale — within the POS communication and regulatory-display boundaries.
names: Create Point Of Purchase (Pop) Promotional Calendar

terms.definition: Create and maintain the site-level marketing calendar — the consolidated marketing activity view per site or site cluster — so sites see one coherent calendar instead of competing programs.

Analyze marketing performance — spend, campaign returns, and customer programs — executing approved measurement methods against the governed measurement frameworks and stewarded metrics, producing the evidence-layer findings that planning and strategy correct from.

Analyze marketing spend — where the money went versus the allocations, with what efficiency across channels, campaigns, and programs — from governed financial data on a stated cost basis, as evidence for allocation and mix decisions.

Analyze campaign returns — outcomes against the measurement hooks each campaign carried, attribution within stated methodological limits, and return on spend — producing campaign-level evidence with assumptions and confidence stated.

Analyze customer programs — loyalty, card, and customer program performance against their design intents — within the privacy controls, as evidence for program design and planning decisions, never as program operation.
Marketing & Sales Operations Management covers channel & partner management, sales execution, pricing, rebates, loyalty/cards, brand standards, compliance, and marketing plan execution.

Manage the company's channel partner relationships — franchisees, licensed-brand providers, dealers, jobbers, and marketers — executing the designed engagement models, coordinating partner qualification and activation through the accountable control owners, reporting partner performance, and developing partner capability.

Manage the ongoing relationships with franchisees under their franchise agreements — engagement, support, performance dialogue, and issue resolution within the agreement's terms — with every change to the legal relationship handled through Legal.
names: Manage Franchisee Relationships Under Franchise Agreements

terms.definition: Manage the ongoing relationships with licensed-brand providers — the parties whose brands the company licenses in, or to whom it licenses out — operating the commercial relationship within the Legal-executed licensing arrangements.
names: Manage Relationship with License Brand Providers

terms.definition: Report franchise and partner performance — volumes, standards conformance, program participation, and relationship health against the measurement frameworks — producing the evidence the relationship management and planning processes act from.

Train and certify franchise site managers against the brand and operating standards — the structured training and certification program that qualifies partner site management to run branded operations — with the standards and mandatory-training regimes owned by their accountable processes.
names: Train and Certify Franchise Site Managers

terms.definition: Execute the sales effort against the plans — pipeline, opportunities, key accounts, quotes, contracts and orders, and non-retail customer serving — as the commercial pursuit whose qualified outcomes are handed to the controlled transaction processes, measured against its own plan.

Manage the sales pipeline — the maintained, staged view of prospects and opportunities across segments and channels — keeping pipeline evidence honest, current, and feeding the forecast-input process.

Manage the key account relationships — executing the account plans for the accounts that matter most, coordinating the company's face to each account, and keeping relationship commitments within the approved commercial frameworks.

Manage each sales opportunity from qualification through pursuit — pursuit strategy, stakeholder engagement, and solution shaping within the approved offers — driving the commercial pursuit to a qualified proceed/no-proceed or handoff outcome.

Develop the commercial quote for a proceeding opportunity — assembling the offer, volume, service, and price content within the approved frameworks — for processing through the quote-and-sale transaction process, creating no binding commitment itself.

Manage the customer's contract-and-order relationship commercially — from accepted quote through contract setup coordination and ongoing order-relationship stewardship — with the transactional contract, order, and fulfillment records owned by the order-to-cash processes.
names: Manage Commercial Contract and Order Relationship

terms.definition: Serve non-retail customers commercially — the standing commercial serving relationship for commercial, industrial, and wholesale customers — maintaining relationship cadence and coordinating resolution while the owning processes execute delivery, service, cases, and billing.

Measure and report sales-execution performance — executing approved sales-performance measures under the relevant measurement frameworks, producing evidence-layer views and variance findings for the planning feedback loops.

Apply the approved pricing architecture in the market — determining posted and transaction sales prices within the approved parameters, corridors, rules, and eligibility, and coordinating their deployment through the accountable master-data and system processes — on the daily and intraday cycles downstream fuel pricing runs on, never modifying the architecture itself.

Determine posted and transaction prices by applying approved price architecture, effective-dated price rules, differentials, indices, corridors, floors, ceilings, customer/channel eligibility, and delegated exception criteria to current permitted inputs.

Implement determined sales prices — submitting approved price changes to the accountable Price Master Data process and coordinating deployment to approved pricing systems, channels, customer communications, and downstream consumers — verifying effective-date, completeness, and audit-trail status.

The process of administering customer and channel-partner rebate arrangements through their operational lifecycle: negotiating individual rebate terms within the approved discount and rebate architecture, implementing agreed arrangements in the systems and procedures that administer them, and settling earned rebates accurately against verified performance.

Negotiate the terms of an individual rebate arrangement with a customer or channel partner — eligibility, performance conditions, rates or tiers, measurement basis, period, and settlement method — within the approved rebate architecture and delegations of authority, obtaining the approvals required before commitment.

Set up an agreed rebate arrangement in the systems and procedures that administer it — configuring terms, measurement and accrual rules, and validation controls — so earned rebates accrue and calculate accurately from the arrangement's effective date.

Calculate, validate, and settle earned rebates at agreed settlement points: verify performance against the arrangement's conditions, compute amounts due, resolve calculation discrepancies with the customer or partner, and prepare the appropriate authorized settlement request in the agreed form.

The process of executing approved marketing plans in market: coordinating and monitoring advertising, promotion and event, and direct-marketing activity according to the released plans, calendars, budgets, and creative deliverables produced by marketing planning, and returning execution and spend actuals for measurement.

Execute released advertising: traffic approved creative to booked media, coordinate and monitor agency and vendor execution within approved media commitments, monitor placement quality and delivery, and capture spend and delivery actuals.

Execute released promotions and events: coordinate site and channel readiness, deploy promotional materials, deliver events, coordinate participating partners, and close out each promotion or event with captured actuals.

Execute released direct-marketing activity: build audience executions from permissioned contactability data, dispatch messages through approved channels, honor preferences and opt-outs, and capture responses for measurement.

A capability that operates loyalty, proprietary-fuel-card, fleet-card, and, where applicable, network-payment-card programs through coordinated but distinct member-program and card-program processes: administering members and cardholders from prospect setup through issuance, servicing, transaction processing, billing coordination, and program benefits, across concurrently running controls for administration, financial coordination, fraud response, compliance, card logistics, and loyalty operation.

Coordinate prospective program-member/cardholder onboarding by capturing applications, validating completeness, and initiating required Credit, KYC, Compliance, Master Data, contract, and program-eligibility controls. Request establishment of governed customer, member, and card-account records through their owning master-data controls, and confirm activation readiness.

Handle cards securely through issuance: coordinate personalization and fulfillment, hold cards in secure custody, deliver cards to customers, and manage return, destruction, and exceptions. Coordinate and evidence quality acceptance, secure custody, delivery, return, destruction, and exception handling according to Security-defined and vendor/scheme requirements.

Detect and respond to suspected fraudulent card activity at program level: monitor transaction alerts, investigate suspected misuse within program authority, block cards and accounts, initiate dispute and chargeback workflows where applicable, and escalate per the enterprise fraud framework.

Manage supplementary services offered through the card program, such as on-road services (breakdown assistance, tolls, parking) and partner services: administer service enrollments, coordinate service-partner delivery, and handle service transactions within the program.

Manage card production runs and periodic reissue cycles: schedule production and personalization with vendors, manage the monthly reissue of expiring cards, and hand produced cards to physical handling for distribution.

Manage acceptance-side payment-card transaction operations where assigned: monitor approved processor/acquirer transaction flows, reconcile transaction submissions and settlement files, prepare exceptions, and coordinate resolution with Treasury, processors, O2C, and Security.

Operate the company's brand loyalty programs: administer member accounts and tiers, operate earn and redemption mechanics according to approved program rules, manage rewards fulfillment and partner benefits, and service member inquiries at program level.

Coordinate card-program billing readiness and program-specific statement requirements; provide validated transaction, account, and presentation data to enterprise invoicing. Manage program-specific presentation such as consolidated statements and itemization, and resolve program-level invoice inquiries.

Administer reimbursements owed under the card program — such as to accepting sites and partners for card transactions or to customers for program credits — validating claims against program terms. Prepare, validate, and submit authorized reimbursement requests or settlement instructions; track status and reconcile program records.

Administer card accounts day to day: process new-card orders, changes to card data such as vehicles, drivers, and purchase restrictions, renewals and replacements, and activations and blocks on customer instruction.

Administer card-level spending and product controls within a customer's approved credit envelope: set and adjust card, driver, or vehicle-level limits and purchase restrictions at customer request or per program rules.

Manage the card program's exposure to non-paying accounts at program level: monitor delinquency signals on card accounts, apply program-level servicing responses such as card blocking, transaction holds, and limit suspension, refer delinquent accounts to collections, and supply program data for bad-debt assessment.
names: Manage Card Delinquency and Collections Referral

terms.definition: Analyze, report, and confirm card transaction activity: validate captured transactions for completeness and accuracy against expected patterns and program terms, confirm transaction sets for billing cycles, and produce transaction reports for customers and internal stakeholders.
names: Analyze, Report, and Confirm Card Transactions

terms.definition: Ensure physical and digital card designs comply with applicable requirements: card scheme and network specifications where applicable, enterprise brand standards, and Security-defined technical and card-media specifications.

Plan consumption of card issuance materials and monitor their inventory. Manage inventory of blank cards, secure card media, carriers, mailers, and issuance materials according to Security-defined inventory and custody controls. Keep production and issuance runs continuously supplied without excess or insecure holdings.
names: Plan Card Stock Consumption and Monitor Inventory

terms.definition: The process of governing brand standards across the branded network: defining and maintaining the standards that govern brand presentation and customer experience at branded sites and channels, verifying conformance through inspection programs, and managing the brand imaging of sites and assets to those standards.

Define, maintain, and publish the brand standards that govern brand presentation and customer experience at branded sites and channels, and verify conformance through inspection programs: plan and conduct inspections where authorized, document findings, agree and track corrective-action plans with the accountable relationship owners, and escalate unresolved or material issues.
names: Manage Brand Standards and Perform Inspection

terms.definition: Manage the brand imaging of sites and assets to approved brand standards: receive standards and network/site pipeline inputs, define and review imaging scope and specifications, coordinate business-case and supplier activity, verify approved work against brand standards, and record conformance and defects.

Manage compliance with commercial obligations in branded sales-network agreements by planning and conducting agreement-based reviews, validating reported sales and other obligation inputs, reporting discrepancies, and routing findings to the accountable relationship, Finance, O2C, Legal, and compliance owners for resolution.

Conduct agreement-based commercial reviews of sales reported by franchisees, dealers, licensees, marketers, and partners; examine supporting records within contractual audit rights; quantify discrepancies affecting contract-based fees, royalties, rebates, contributions, or commitments; and route findings for financial, relationship, legal, or corrective resolution.
names: Conduct Audit To Validate Reported Sales
Conduct Commercial Audit to Validate Reported Sales

terms.definition: Order Management is the end-to-end process that addresses all aspects of collecting cash - from initial order receipt & credit authorization to collections & revenue assurance activities.

The capability that stewards the governed commercial master data on which sales, pricing, fulfillment, billing, and service transactions depend — customer, price and discount, product and service, tax, and location/site records, together with the workflow configurations and commercial policy content that control how they change — maintaining each domain as validated, effective-dated, auditable records through concurrent stewardship processes.
names: Manage Master Data (Customer, Price, Product, Tax, Location)

terms.definition: Maintain governed Party, Customer Account, account-role, hierarchy, address/location-reference, contact, commercial attribute, and relationship records as defined by the approved customer domain model. A customer master record may represent a party, account, role, relationship, or system-specific record according to the governed model; it must not collapse Sold-To, Bill-To, Payer, Ship-To, Loading-Authorized Party, dealer, distributor, or marketer meanings. Create, validate, update, deduplicate, and retire these records on authorized submissions, keeping them accurate, unique within the governed model, and consumable by sales, fulfillment, billing, credit, and service processes.
names: Maintain Customer and Commercial Account Master Data

terms.definition: Maintain governed price and discount records: validate and apply authorized price, discount, and rebate-condition submissions with correct effective-dating, maintain price structures and condition records, and assure the completeness, consistency, and auditability of the pricing data consumed by quoting, ordering, and billing.

Maintain governed product and service master records: create and update records, attributes, units of measure, classifications, and hierarchies on authorized submissions from the accountable product owners, keeping the catalog accurate and consumable by pricing, ordering, fulfillment, and billing.
names: Maintain Product and Service Master Data

terms.definition: Maintain governed tax master records as directed by the accountable tax owners, with effective-dating aligned to legal effectivity, so that taxability determination and tax calculation in transactions consume current, authorized tax data.

Maintain the governed workflow configurations that control commercial transactions and master-data changes — approval chains, routing rules, thresholds, and escalation paths — keeping them aligned with approved delegations of authority and process designs, tested, versioned, and auditable.

Maintain commercial policy content and system-consumable policy parameters as governed reference content. Formal policy approval, legal review, corporate publication, retention schedule, and enterprise document-management controls remain with the accountable governance and document-management owners. Administer, publish, version, and distribute the commercial policy content and parameters that transactions and workflows reference — terms frameworks, condition catalogs, policy parameters — keeping the published version identical to the approved one.
names: Maintain Commercial Policy Content and Approved Parameters

terms.definition: Coordinate the onboarding of a new customer of any type, from the setup request to a customer that is set up in every system that uses it.

The capability that turns approved prices, policies, and credit decisions into governed customer commercial arrangements: establishing commercial terms and customer-facing frameworks, issuing quotes and renewals, planning and monitoring commercial revenue, defining offered financing and payment methods, analyzing customer profitability, and operating the customer self-service portal — concurrent commercial controls in O2C operations.
names: Manage Commercial Terms, Quoting, and Customer Commercial Services

terms.definition: Establish the durable commercial arrangements under which customers transact: negotiate and establish master agreements, terms frameworks, and customer-specific commercial terms within approved policies and delegations, coordinate legal review and execution, and have executed terms recorded into governed systems so downstream transactions apply them automatically.

Formally issue customer quotes and manage renewals through governed systems: produce quotes from approved prices, established terms, and the approved quote content requirements; manage validity periods, revisions, and versioning; and run contract-anchored renewal cycles so expiring arrangements are re-quoted and re-executed on time.

Develop the commercial revenue plan — the monetized operating outlook of the agreed sales plan by customer, channel, product, and period — and monitor actual revenue against it, analyzing deviations and routing findings to the accountable owners according to cause.
names: Develop and Monitor Commercial Revenue Plan

terms.definition: Define the approved financing options, payment methods, payment-term menus, eligibility conditions, and customer-facing commercial rules that may be offered within Treasury-approved instruments, Credit-approved exposure rules, Tax/Legal requirements, and delegated authorities.

Analyze the profitability of customers, accounts, channels, and segments: apply Finance-approved costing and allocation methods to revenue, cost-to-serve, terms, rebate, and credit data to produce profitability views and insights that inform pricing strategy, terms decisions, credit reviews, and account management.

Operate the customer self-service portal as a governed commercial channel: manage portal content and functions, coordinate customer access and business entitlements through Security-defined services, and route every portal transaction and inquiry into its accountable process.

The process of managing customer orders through their commercial lifecycle: capturing and validating orders against governed controls, allocating and releasing them per approved rules, coordinating fulfillment through the accountable physical operations, handling changes, cancellations, and returns, and tracking the order book through to completed, evidenced fulfillment ready for invoicing.

Capture customer orders from all approved channels — portal, EDI, phone, direct entry — and validate each against governed controls: resolve the correct party and account roles, confirm product, price, terms, and tax from governed master data, apply credit checks, verify loading and delivery authorizations, and accept, hold, or reject the order accordingly.

Allocate available product and supply capacity to validated orders and release allocated orders to the physical scheduling and fulfillment processes. Apply approved allocation rules, including contractual commitments, approved priority classes, fairness rules, regulatory/safety obligations, and authorized shortage/disruption procedures.

Process authenticated order change and cancellation requests: validate the request against the order's status and the applicable cutoff rules, re-run affected validations (price, credit, allocation, tax) for changes, apply approved change and cancellation fees per policy, and propagate the outcome to allocation, fulfillment, billing, and the customer.

Coordinate released orders through physical fulfillment to evidenced completion: hand orders to the accountable scheduling and logistics processes, monitor fulfillment progress, manage commercial exceptions — shortages, substitutions, partial deliveries — per approved rules, receive, link, validate for commercial completeness, and retain fulfillment evidence supplied by physical processes, and confirm completed fulfillments to billing.

Track the order book end to end — status, aging, exceptions, and completion across all open orders — and maintain the rolling short-horizon operational forecast of expected order volumes and timing that scheduling and supply processes plan against.
names: Track Order Book and Forecast Order Volumes
Track Orders and Forecast Order Book

terms.definition: Manage commercial return authorization and coordination; it does not determine product disposition, direct hazardous-product transport, issue a credit memo, or authorize a refund. Validate return requests against policy and the original order, coordinate authorized physical return through the accountable logistics and quality processes, route product disposition to its owners, and hand financial credit to the billing controls.
names: Manage Commercial Returns Authorization and Coordination

terms.definition: The capability that owns customer credit and counterparty risk in commercial operations: maintaining credit policies that encode the approved risk appetite, establishing customer credit limits and risk codes, monitoring exposure against limits continuously, analyzing portfolio credit risk, deciding credit-driven closure and reinstatement of commercial eligibility, and executing KYC due diligence — the decision home for every credit control the commercial processes apply.

Maintain the credit policies that govern customer credit: encode the Finance-approved risk appetite into credit standards, terms eligibility rules, security requirements, hold/release rules, and delegation thresholds; keep policies current with experience and conditions; and publish them through governed policy content for consistent application.

Decide customer-level credit: assess creditworthiness from KYC outcomes, financial statements, bureau data, payment history, parent support and credit-support instruments, and industry, geography, product, and channel risk; establish credit limits, risk codes, terms eligibility, and required security (guarantees, letters of credit, prepayment, deposits) per policy and the delegations of authority; and record decisions to governed master data with effective dates and review schedules.

Monitor customer credit exposure against approved limits continuously: calculate exposure per approved policy, aggregate it across the customer's accounts per the governed credit hierarchy, apply and release holds under authorized rules and decisions, and route deterioration signals to limit review, servicing, and collections.

Analyze credit risk at portfolio level: concentration by customer, sector, channel, and geography; aging and risk-code migration; loss experience and expected-loss signals; and stress indicators under changing market conditions — producing insights that inform credit policies, limit strategies, and Finance's reserve and allowance determinations.

Determine and coordinate credit-driven suspension, closure, or reinstatement of commercial eligibility under approved policy. It does not dissolve a legal entity, unilaterally terminate contracts, extinguish debt, delete master data, or prevent Legal/Commercial owners from managing non-credit exits. Coordinate the closure or reinstatement workflow through the owning processes so records, orders, cards, collections, and contracts land consistently.
names: Perform Credit-Driven Customer Closure and Reinstatement

terms.definition: Execute know-your-customer due diligence: verify customer identity and legal existence, collect, verify, and maintain beneficial-ownership information where required by applicable policy, law, regulation, customer type, or risk rating, screen customers and counterparties against sanctions and watchlists, assess KYC risk per the enterprise framework, and refresh due diligence on the required cycles and trigger events.

The capability that operates commercial customer service: receiving and prioritizing customer requests, inquiries, and complaints from all channels, resolving directly what governed data and approved documentation can answer, routing the substance of everything else to its owning process, maintaining the case record end to end, following up to confirmed resolution, running the customer service-review cadence, and delivering customer training from approved content.

Assign priority to each incoming customer request, inquiry, or complaint per the approved prioritization framework, and maintain that framework current with service experience. Priority is assigned using an approved framework that may include safety/regulatory escalation, customer impact, service commitment, financial/commercial impact, vulnerability/criticality, operational impact, recurrence, and required response time.
names: Establish Priority Assignment of Customer Request/Inquiry

terms.definition: Maintain governed operational case and interaction records for customer requests, inquiries, complaints, and service communications, including categorization, ownership, status, timestamps, routing, correspondence, evidence links, resolution outcome, and retention classification.
names: Maintain Customer Request and Inquiry Records
Maintain Requests and Inquiries Master Database

terms.definition: Work each customer request or inquiry to resolution: answer directly what governed data and approved content can answer — status, information, and documentation requests — route the substance of everything else to its owning process with the case attached, track routed items to outcome, and communicate resolution to the customer.

Follow up resolved cases with the customer: confirm the resolution held, verify commitments made during resolution were met, capture satisfaction and residual issues, and reopen or re-route where resolution failed.

Conduct structured periodic service reviews with customers: review service performance against commitments, open items and their paths to closure, complaint and issue trends, and agreed improvement actions, with tracked follow-through. Review cadence may be quarterly by default and adjusted by customer tier, agreement, issue profile, regulatory obligation, or service model.

Provide customers training on commercial tools, portals, ordering, documentation, card-program administration, and approved product/service interaction procedures. Where the program includes safe-handling orientation, the content is delivered exactly from approved Product Stewardship/EHS materials; it is not safety certification, regulatory training authority, or site-operator training unless a separate accountable framework expressly delegates that role. Develop delivery materials from approved content, deliver through appropriate formats, and track completion where required.
Operational Accounting includes processes that denotes the ledger like capability leveraged by the users for the ease of auditing and record keeping.

The process of billing customers for delivered products and services: creating and distributing invoices from confirmed evidence and governed commercial data, determining transaction taxes per the Tax function's determinations, accounting for customer self-billing under executed agreements, and issuing every correction — credit memos, exception invoices, reversals, and rebills — as controlled document events.

Create customer invoices from confirmed channel evidence and governed commercial data on the customer's billing cadence — per delivery, consolidated, statement, or cycle — and distribute them through the customer's channels in the formats and content the applicable requirements mandate.

Account for customer self-billing arrangements: receive customer-issued billing documents under executed self-billing agreements, validate each against confirmed fulfillment evidence and governed prices and terms, record the validated self-bill, and resolve differences with the customer per the agreement.

Determine the taxes applicable to each billed transaction. Apply tax determination rules through effective-dated tax master data, transaction attributes, product tax classes, origin/destination or jurisdiction logic, customer tax status, exemption evidence, and other Tax-approved rules. Produce the tax lines the invoice carries, including federal and state fuel excise treatment where applicable.

Create controlled credit memos on authorized instruction: validate the instructing process's authorization and documented basis, reference the original invoice, apply the applicable approvals per the delegations of authority, issue the credit memo, and record its complete linkage from instruction to settlement effect.

Correct billing through controlled document events: validate the correction's basis and authorization, and create the proper controlled document type under approved rules — full cancellation, partial correction, replacement/rebill, debit adjustment, tax-only correction, or exception invoice — with coded reasons and the applicable approvals, preserving the complete original-to-correction chain.
names: Manage Invoice Exceptions, Reversals, and Rebilling

terms.definition: The process of turning billed transactions into accounted revenue and settled receivables: Record and process receipt notifications, bank/lockbox/acquirer settlement information, remittance evidence, and accounting events relating to customer payments received through Treasury-managed arrangements. Capture remittance information, apply receipts against governed receivables, manage unapplied and exception items to resolution, reconcile receivables against bank and processor settlement information and the general ledger, and perform revenue accounting under Finance-approved policy.
names: Manage Cash Application, A/R & Revenue Accounting

terms.definition: Record customer payment receipts daily: capture receipt notifications and settlement information from Treasury-managed banking, lockbox, card-acquirer, and electronic arrangements across the approved payment methods, validate completeness against the receipt-source reports, and stage receipts for application with their identifying data.
names: Record Customer Receipts and Payment Notifications

terms.definition: Capture and normalize customer remittance information from all formats — EDI, portal, email, paper, bank addenda — validate it for completeness and consistency, link it to the receipts it explains, and stage the combined evidence for application.

Apply staged receipts against open governed receivables daily: match on remittance evidence and approved application rules, apply exact matches, resolve tolerable differences per approved tolerance rules, route short-pays, over-pays, and claimed deductions to their owning processes, and post applications with complete linkage.

Own the exception state for cash that cannot be applied: research unidentified and unapplied receipts, contact customers through the service channels, resolve each item within policy time bounds — application, refund request, or other authorized disposition — and maintain aged visibility of everything unresolved.

Reconcile the receivables and receipts positions daily: bank and lockbox reporting to recorded receipts, card-acquirer and processor settlement files to recorded transactions and receipts, subledger activity to applications, and provide the reconciled positions that feed general-ledger reconciliation and period-end close.
names: Perform Cash, Acquirer, and Receivables Reconciliations

terms.definition: Execute revenue accounting under Finance-approved policy: recognize revenue as performance obligations are satisfied per the approved recognition model, account for deferred and unbilled revenue, coordinate revenue-affecting accruals with the accrual processes, enforce revenue cutoff, and deliver revenue accounting into period-end close.

The capability that resolves what customers owe but have not paid: adjudicating disputed billed amounts against the evidence chain, collecting undisputed overdue receivables under the approved collection strategy, executing Finance-approved expected-credit-loss estimation and write-off processes, and turning dispute and collection patterns into root-cause action plans with the owning processes — concurrent controls with distinct authorities and cadences.

Adjudicate disputed billed amounts: capture and classify disputes from all routes, investigate each against the evidence chain — billing documents, fulfillment and custody evidence, contracts and terms, tax determinations, credit memo and adjustment evidence, and applicable commercial policy — decide validity under the delegations of authority, and instruct the outcome: credit-memo or correction instruction for valid disputes, release to collection for invalid ones, with the customer informed through the service communication loop.

Execute the approved collection strategy on undisputed, due receivables: run dunning and contact cycles by segment and aging, secure and track payment commitments, administer payment plans within pre-approved authority, escalate through the approved ladder to third-party agencies or legal referral, and keep the collection record complete.

Execute Finance-approved expected-credit-loss estimation and write-off processes for trade receivables, using approved methodology, portfolio inputs, collection status, and forward-looking assumptions; prepare and record allowance and write-off outcomes under the applicable Finance delegation.

Turn dispute, deduction, and collection patterns into prevention: analyze the reason-coded evidence the resolution processes produce, identify root causes, develop action plans with the accountable owning processes, and track agreed actions to verified closure.
names: Develop Root-Cause Analyses and Action Plans

terms.definition: The capability that closes and evidences O2C's books and obligations: running period-end processing on the Finance calendar, reconciling receivables to the general ledger with control evidence, analyzing and calculating accruals, reconciling and preparing indirect-tax reporting, preparing taxability-treatment recommendations for Tax approval, executing intercompany invoicing per approved transfer-pricing policies, and administering royalty, brand-fee, and contribution streams under executed agreements.
names: Manage Accounting, Regulatory Reporting and Compliance

terms.definition: Run O2C period-end close on the Finance-approved calendar: verify completeness and reconciliation evidence from every feeding process, process period-end adjustments under approved authority, enforce cutoff across billing, receipts, accruals, and corrections, and deliver the closed O2C position into Finance's consolidation with its evidence chain.

Reconcile the receivables subledger to the general ledger each period, resolve reconciling items through their owning processes, maintain the evidence that the O2C financial controls operated as designed, and support internal and external audit with governed records.
