Analyze and calculate the O2C accruals each period under Finance-approved methodologies: rebate and discount accruals, returns and allowances, loyalty liabilities, unbilled revenue and costs, variable consideration, promotional and brand-fund obligations, royalty and fee liabilities, and freight and service charges where applicable — delivering calculated, evidenced accruals and true-ups into close.

Reconcile O2C indirect taxes each period and prepare their reporting: reconcile transaction tax lines and governed tax data to the amounts reportable and remittable by tax type and jurisdiction — excise, sales and use, VAT/GST as applicable — prepare returns and reports per the Tax function's direction, and support remittance through the authorized payment process.

Assess and prepare taxability-treatment recommendations for Tax approval, including new or changed product, channel, jurisdiction, exemption, and exception classes; evaluate reporting/remittance implications; and coordinate approved treatment changes into governed tax data and procedures.
names: Determine Taxability for Tax Compliance and Reporting

terms.definition: Execute intercompany invoicing between legal entities: invoice intercompany product transfers, services, and charges per the approved transfer-pricing policies and executed intercompany agreements, on the approved cycles, with the evidence and documentation the policies require, and support Finance's reconciliation, elimination, and consolidation.

Administer the royalty, brand-fee, and contribution streams owed under franchise, license, and partner agreements: compute amounts due from validated reported sales and agreement terms, invoice them through the billing controls, track and support their collection through the receivables processes, apply audit-finding adjustments, and account for administered funds per the agreements and Finance's treatment.
names: Administer Royalty, Brand Fee, and Contribution Streams
Manage Collection of Royalty and Fees

terms.definition: Customer service & support consist of processes such as all support & service offerings to consumers & business partners both from a conceptual & operational view. It ranges from defining the methods of interaction (e.g., on site, call center, web), along defining, setting up & operating facilities & technology down to managing service staff.

The capability that builds and runs the machinery of commercial service and support: defining the service operating model, managing day-to-day service operations, and managing the workforce, facilities, technology, and contact-center channel the service processes run on.

Define and maintain the service operating model. The model defines service scope, channels, operating hours, service tiers, escalation paths, roles, service-level design assumptions, and knowledge/procedure requirements. Contractually committed service levels require commercial-terms approval and cannot be created solely by the operating model. Approved through the accountable governance and published as controlled content.

Run the service operation day to day: plan and schedule capacity against demand, balance workload across teams and channels, monitor operational quality and service-level attainment in real time, and manage operational incidents and escalations within the operating model.

Manage the service workforce operationally: plan staffing against forecast demand, schedule and roster within applicable rules, maintain skills and readiness through training coordination, and support the workforce day to day — all within the HR-owned employment frameworks.

Manage service locations from the occupant side: define space and workplace needs, coordinate readiness, upkeep requests, and moves with the corporate facilities owners, and coordinate safety and access compliance with EHS and Security at service sites.

Own the service operation's technology from the business side: define requirements and business configuration for service platforms (case, telephony, knowledge, workforce tools), drive adoption and fit-for-purpose use, and feed the service capability roadmap — with IT owning the platforms themselves.

Operate the contact-center channel for commercial service: manage capacity, queues, and routing across voice and digital contact channels, run channel operations to the service levels, monitor interaction quality, and provide the channel through which the customer-request processes work.

The capability that executes commercial service work: maintaining the data service delivery runs on, managing the customer interaction during delivery, and fulfilling service events routed from the request capability — concurrent delivery controls operating through to evidenced completion.

Maintain the operational data service delivery runs on: entitlement and coverage data, installed-base and service-history records, appointments, service tasks, and service-event data — captured and verified at delivery time, linked to the governed case and customer records.

Manage the customer interaction during service delivery: identify and verify the customer per the Security-defined controls, set expectations from confirmed information, keep the customer informed through service notices during the event, and confirm completion.
names: Manage Customer Interactions in Service Delivery

terms.definition: Fulfill individual service events end to end: receive the routed event with its case linkage, verify entitlement from governed delivery data, execute the service work per the applicable agreement and procedures, capture completion evidence, and return the outcome to the case and — where billable — to billing.

The process of measuring the service operation on a recurring cycle: infrastructure and channel performance, workforce operational performance, and overall service effectiveness — consolidated into an integrated service performance view.

Measure the performance of the service infrastructure from the business perspective: facilities fitness, technology and platform performance, and contact-channel performance — as evidence for the accountable owners.

Measure workforce operational performance in the service operation — handle times, quality scores, utilization, schedule adherence, readiness — as evidence for capacity planning, training, and service improvement.

Measure overall service effectiveness: resolution outcomes, service-level attainment, customer satisfaction and effort through governed measurement, and cost-effectiveness per Finance-approved methods — informing the operating model and the accountable owners.

Information Technology Includes Processes Related To Providing IT Support Across Commercial Operations. It Covers Strategy, Delivery & Governance Processes. Commercial Information Technology Includes Hardware, Software & Communication Infrastructure.

The operating businesses and value-chain domains in scope for the enterprise's downstream oil and gas model: Commercial & Marketing, Refining, and the Midstream transportation, terminaling, storage, and bulk-logistics activities that support downstream supply, distribution, and delivery of hydrocarbon feedstocks and refined products.

The enterprise functions in scope that enable, govern, control, support, and provide shared services to the downstream operating businesses: Supply Chain Management, Finance, Shared Services, Process Excellence & IT, Human Resources, Legal & Corporate Communications, and Environment, Health, Safety & Government Reporting.

Protect people, assets, and the environment through process safety; occupational health and safety; environmental management and compliance; emergency preparedness and response; incident, release, and near-miss management; corrective-action learning; and required regulatory reporting to government authorities.

Planning, recording, controlling, reporting, and managing the financial resources, performance, obligations, and risks of the downstream business, including financial planning and analysis, accounting, reporting, payroll, treasury, tax, and internal financial controls.

The function that plans, attracts, develops, rewards, engages, retains, and transitions the workforce to enable the downstream business, including workforce planning, talent acquisition, onboarding, learning and development, performance management, compensation and benefits, employee and labor relations, HR policy and compliance, workforce information, and HR service delivery.

Provide legal counsel and legal-risk management, including contract and transaction support, litigation and dispute resolution, regulatory and compliance advice, corporate governance and entity support, and management of external legal providers; develop and deliver internal corporate communications and approved enterprise messaging.
The transportation, terminaling, storage, and bulk handling of crude oil, intermediates, and refined products between supply points, refineries, terminals, and downstream distribution locations.

The enabling function that drives operational excellence through process governance, standardization, performance management, continuous improvement, and transformation; and enables the enterprise through technology strategy, architecture, platforms, infrastructure, cybersecurity, data and integration, and digital capabilities.

The operation of petroleum refineries to convert crude oil and other hydrocarbon feedstocks into specification-compliant fuels, blendstocks, lubricants, asphalt, petrochemical feedstocks, and other refined products through separation, conversion, treatment, blending, and associated refinery operations.

An enterprise service-delivery model that consolidates common, repeatable business-support services for multiple business units, legal entities, or regions through a shared organization, standardized processes, common platforms, and defined service levels.

The integrated planning, coordination, and optimization of feedstock, intermediate, product, inventory, capacity, logistics, and information flows across the downstream petroleum value chain — from supply and sourcing through refining, terminaling, distribution, and customer fulfilment.

The Finance-owned capability that establishes and operates the financial planning and performance-management framework; coordinates, consolidates, challenges, validates, publishes, monitors, and refreshes enterprise and business-unit financial plans and budgets in accordance with the approved planning calendar, planning assumptions, delegated authorities, and financial-control requirements; and measures and reports financial performance against those plans.

The Refining capability that coordinates refinery availability, asset-condition and integrity inputs, maintenance and turnaround windows, production-plan impacts, readiness, and recovery interfaces so refinery performance objectives can be planned and managed against approved maintenance, integrity, and turnaround commitments.
names: Refinery Asset Reliability and Turnaround Coordination

terms.definition: The Refining-owned capability that coordinates refinery performance oversight and site-level business-risk management, including the identification, assessment, treatment coordination, monitoring, and escalation of risks that may affect refinery objectives.
Provide pipeline transportation of crude oil, refined products and other hydrocarbons to shippers under transportation agreements and tariffs.
Set up and maintain the transportation service agreements, committed volumes and tariff rates the provider offers affiliated and third-party shippers.
names: Manage Pipeline Service Agreements and Tariffs

terms.definition: Accept shipper nominations, schedule batches and run the movements through the pipeline system.
Measure the barrels received and delivered, apply the tariff, and bill each shipper for the throughput and any shortfall against committed volumes.
names: Measure Pipeline Throughput and Bill Transportation

terms.definition: Provide the receipt, storage, throughput, blending and delivery of products at terminals for affiliated and third-party customers.
Set up and maintain the terminal service agreements, committed throughput and fees the provider offers its customers.
Record each customer's receipts, deliveries and blending at the terminal and bill the fees due under its agreement.
names: Account for Terminal Throughput and Bill Services

terms.definition: Provide marine transportation of crude oil and products with towboats and barges for refineries and terminals.
Keep the towboat and barge fleet available for the planned voyages: deployment, maintenance windows and charters in or out.
Set up and maintain the marine transportation agreements and bill the voyages and fees due under them.
names: Manage Marine Service Agreements and Billing

terms.definition: Provide tank storage for crude oil and products to affiliated and third-party customers.
Allocate tank capacity to customers under their storage agreements and track capacity committed and available.
Bill each customer the storage fees and any throughput or excess charges due under its agreement.
Agree which units come down, for how long, and what the outage does to throughput, yields, product supply and margin.
names: Define Turnaround Scope and Business Impacts

terms.definition: Fit each turnaround window into the plan across refineries and units: its timing and sequence, the supply cover and inventory builds around it, and the moves of intermediate products to units that keep running.
names: Coordinate Turnaround Schedule and Commercial Plan

terms.definition: Track the turnaround against its planned dates and duration, and adjust supply, sales and the plan when it runs long or short.
names: Monitor Execution and Manage Commercial Impacts

terms.definition: Agree the restart date, ramp-up rates and time to on-specification product that the plan and the schedule use, and update them as the restart proceeds.
Compare the turnaround's cost, duration and lost margin with plan, and feed the lessons into the next turnaround plan.
names: Reconcile Turnaround Costs and Review Performance

terms.definition: For a given planning cycle, Produce Demand Forecast (CM-1-1-1-1) completes approval and release of the demand-forecast version before Regional Optimization (CM-1-1-2) uses that version as an approved planning input. Forecasting and optimization remain iterative across versions and cycles.
names: Produce Demand Forecast before Regional Optimization, per forecast version

terms.definition: For a given forecast cycle and version, Publish Forecast and Generate Component Level Forecast Plan (CM-1-1-1-1-4) publishes and makes the approved forecast available before Regional Optimization (CM-1-1-2) uses that version as an approved planning input. Other optimization work may proceed independently; subsequent forecast revisions can prompt another optimization run.
names: Publish Forecast and Generate Component Level Forecast Plan before Regional Optimization, per forecast version

terms.definition: For each replenishment requirement or approved revision, Manage Inventory Replenishment (CM-1-1-3-7-9) establishes and releases the required product, quantity, destination, and timing before Physical Distribution Scheduling (CM-1-1-3-6) schedules the corresponding movement. Scheduling constraints may feed back into a revised replenishment requirement.
names: Manage Inventory Replenishment before Physical Distribution Scheduling, per replenishment requirement

terms.definition: For each scheduling horizon, Refinery Planning and Optimization (CM-1-1-4) makes the applicable approved plan or authorized revision available before Production Scheduling (CM-1-1-7-2) releases the corresponding executable schedule. Scheduling preparation may overlap planning, and feasibility feedback may trigger plan revisions.
names: Refinery Planning and Optimization before Production Scheduling, per scheduling horizon

terms.definition: For each plan-selection decision that uses scenario analysis, Perform Scenario Analysis (CM-1-1-4-7-8) provides the relevant evaluated alternatives before the corresponding production plan is selected and approved within Refinery Planning and Optimization (CM-1-1-4). This is an internal step-level sequence, not a sequence preceding the start of the parent process.
names: Perform Scenario Analysis before Refinery Planning and Optimization, per plan-selection decision

terms.definition: Perform Lease Actualization (CM-1-2-3-1-6) follows establishment of the applicable effective lease-contract terms and required division-of-interest references maintained under Manage Lease Contract (CM-1-2-1-2-8), applying them to the relevant delivery or production period. Subsequent changes and corrections are handled through controlled updates.
names: Manage Lease Contract before Perform Lease Actualization, per delivery period

terms.definition: For trade-linked physical movements, Actualizations (CM-1-2-3-1) follows initial Trade Capture (CM-1-2-1-3), using the captured trade and associated movement references to record and validate actual quantities and other applicable movement facts. Subsequent amendments and corrections remain controlled.
names: Trade Capture before Actualizations, per physical movement

terms.definition: Where a power transaction involves a separately captured transmission arrangement, Capture Transmission Deals (CM-1-2-1-3-11) records the applicable terms before Settle Power (CM-1-2-4-1-15) calculates or validates the associated transmission-related charges. Other power-settlement activities may proceed independently.
names: Capture Transmission Deals before Settle Power, per transaction

terms.definition: Where ISO/power-pool settlement includes items arising from a captured transmission arrangement, initial capture of the relevant arrangement under Capture Transmission Deals (CM-1-2-1-3-11) precedes validation of those items under Settle ISO/Power Pools (CM-1-2-4-1-7). Other settlement activities may proceed independently.
names: Capture Transmission Deals before Settle ISO/Power Pools, per transaction

terms.definition: Capture Physical Trades (CM-1-2-1-3-3) records the agreed commercial terms and makes the required trade data available to Confirmations Management (CM-1-2-2-2) for prompt counterparty confirmation. Initial capture precedes submission for confirmation; discrepancies may require controlled correction of the captured record.
names: Capture Physical Trades before Confirmations Management, per transaction

terms.definition: Capture Storage Deals (CM-1-2-1-3-5) records the agreed storage-service terms before those terms are used by Settle Terminal/Storage (CM-1-2-4-1-14) to calculate and validate applicable charges. Settlement follows the agreement’s billing schedule and may occur periodically or in advance while the contract and storage operations remain active.
names: Capture Storage Deals before Settle Terminal/Storage, per transaction

terms.definition: Capture Financial (OTC) Trades (CM-1-2-1-3-7) records the agreed transaction terms and makes the required trade data available to Confirmations Management (CM-1-2-2-2) for prompt counterparty confirmation. Initial capture precedes submission for confirmation; discrepancies and subsequent amendments are handled through controlled correction and confirmation procedures.
names: Capture Financial (OTC) Trades before Confirmations Management, per transaction

terms.definition: Settle Financial OTC Trades (CM-1-2-4-1-11) follows initial Capture Financial (OTC) Trades (CM-1-2-1-3-7), using the captured transaction terms and applicable settlement-period inputs to calculate and validate payment obligations, subject to the required confirmation, reconciliation, and authorization controls.
names: Capture Financial (OTC) Trades before Settle Financial OTC Trades, per transaction

terms.definition: For each physical delivery or settlement period, Actualizations (CM-1-2-3-1) records and validates the relevant actual quantities and movement facts before Settlements (CM-1-2-4-1) uses those inputs to calculate or validate the corresponding charges. Settlement preparation and contractually permitted provisional billing may proceed before every input is final; subsequent corrections are handled through controlled true-ups.
names: Actualizations before Settlements, per delivery period

terms.definition: Manage AR/AP & Actuals (CM-1-2-4-2-4) follows the applicable settlement calculation and invoice validation under Settlements (CM-1-2-4-1) when posting the corresponding receivable, payable, or adjustment. Accruals and other financial-actuals activities may proceed independently; subsequent settlement changes are reflected through controlled adjustments.
names: Settlements before Manage AR/AP & Actuals, per posting

terms.definition: Demurrage Management (CM-1-2-4-4) precedes the claim-specific posting activities within Manage AR/AP & Actuals (CM-1-2-4-2-4) by providing the calculated, validated, and authorized demurrage amount and supporting references. Subsequent claim revisions are reflected through controlled accounting adjustments; unrelated AR/AP activity proceeds independently.
names: Demurrage Management before Manage AR/AP & Actuals, per demurrage claim

terms.definition: For each customer quote or renewal version whose composition is owned by Develop Quote (CM-1-3-6-2-4), that version is developed and receives the required authorization before Issue Quotes & Renewals (CM-1-3-7-2-2) issues it to the customer. Preparatory issuance activities may proceed in parallel; revised versions repeat the applicable development and authorization steps.
names: Develop Quote before Issue Quotes & Renewals, per quote version

terms.definition: A named, governed set of data that a business area publishes for others to use, defined by what it covers. A definition, never the data: the platforms that hold the data product hold its records.
The two kinds of data product, told apart by what they are built from and what logic they add.
A group of related data products in one segment of the portfolio, such as Energy Trading & Risk Management.
The portfolio's segments, data product lines and data products, as one hierarchy: a data product's skos:broader is its line, and a line's is its segment.
The layers of the decision owner's data platform, in their names, each built from the one before.
A value column of a platform table, recorded only where its lineage is recorded: the price columns.

A platform table or view that is published as a governed data product, as part of a data product of the portfolio, and classified as foundational or derived. A replica table is a platform table but not a platform data product: it copies a system's own records.
A table or view on a data platform, named by its full name (catalog, schema and name), in one layer of the platform: replica, silver, gold or metric view. A definition of the table, never its rows.
The platform tables and views the module names, as a flat list.
One of the portfolio's top-level groups of data product lines: Commercial, Midstream or Corporate. Each is anchored in a part of the process map.
The three statuses the portfolio schema allows a data product or line. The portfolio uses two of them.
The part of the process map a segment's data products serve, from the portfolio's process-domain reference. Context, not ownership.
Why the data product has its kind, in a sentence.
The criterion of the data product kind code list that decided the kind: inputs or logic.
The column's name, as the table spells it.
The table the column belongs to.
A process that uses the data product's data as an input. Context for where the data is used, not ownership.
The operational system whose own records a replica table copies.
Whether the data product is foundational or derived, from the data product kind code list.
A system the view's lineage reaches, through the replicas of that system's records.
The table's or view's full name on its platform: catalog, schema and name.
A governed data product built from one or more other data products, adding business logic (aggregation, calculation, measures or a model for a use case) for a known group of consumers.

A governed data product that publishes the facts or master data of one business domain, built only from the operational systems of record, with transformations limited to cleansing, validation, conforming and identity resolution, and not modelled for a particular consumer.
The platform layer the table is in, from the layer code list.
Tables that join and calculate silver data for a known group of consumers.
A view that defines measures, once, over a gold or silver table, which consumers such as Genie agents query.
A copy of an operational system's own tables, as the system holds them.
Cleansed and conformed tables of one domain's facts (UDM) and master data dimensions (MDM), built from replicas.
Data products supporting physical/financial trading and commercial risk management (ETRM domain).
Pricing structures, logistics execution, margin and external market data products.
Customer-facing marketing and sales data products.
Value chain planning and optimization data products. Referenced as 'P&O' (a product line, not a portfolio item).
Whether the portfolio describes the data product or line (active), only names it (defined only), or leaves a decision about it open, from the portfolio status code list.
The process whose work creates the data product's data, named by a recorded decision or the process authority. A data product with no producing process has no owning process (competency question 7).
Backcast results vs plan/perfect-foresight, value leakage, and continuous improvement data.
Brand, branded-site, and brand-partner data integration.
Commodity trading risk data: positions, exposures, P&L, VaR, limits, counterparty credit in the trading context. Distinct from Order-to-Cash customer AR credit.
The governed customer master: the customer records, accounts and their attributes that the systems which serve customers share.
Third-party market feeds: price assessments, indices, market intelligence inputs.
Refinery/local production planning and crude scheduling data.
Nominations, scheduling, and physical movement execution data (pipeline, marine, rail, truck from the commercial view).
Custody transfer, gain/loss, and shrinkage data across movements and terminal operations.
Validated price system of record: official product prices derived from market data and internal assessment.
Margin measurement data across commercial operations (supply, logistics, channel).
Deal/trade facts for physical commodity transactions: trade capture, contracts, positions, movements context.
Product avails and allocation decisions data supporting order validation and channel supply.
Product/crude quality data: assays, lab results, specifications, blending quality outcomes.
Wholesale rack price data: calculated, approved, published rack prices per sales cycle. Distinct portfolio from Master Pricing.
Regional optimization and distribution planning data.
Retail transaction and payment data captured at branded retail sites (tender, cards, loyalty-linked payment).
True when the table is in a sandbox catalog, not production; its name changes when the production name is recorded.
Commercial hydrocarbon data domains: trading, marketing & sales, market structure & logistics, planning & optimization.
Corporate/enabling function data domains. Maps loosely to the Enabling Functions L0 in the MPC map (all L1 stubs).

Midstream operations data domains. Since 2026-10-18 the map decomposes Midstream as fuels logistics (MS 1: pipeline, terminal, marine and storage services, the decision of 2026-10-18); the portfolios below are not yet linked to those processes.
A measure of the kpi module whose values the metric view gives: the binding a consumer follows to quote a value (the decision of 2026-10-19, as amended by the decision of 2026-10-25, item 6).
The portfolio describes the data product or line, and it is in use.
The portfolio names the data product or line but does not describe it. Its definition waits for its data owners.
A decision about the data product or line is open.

The evidence order the repository applies: the process authority and the decision owner's own material, then Marathon Petroleum, then U.S. refining peers, then industry and regulatory sources, then generic frameworks as support only.
The tier of the evidence order a source belongs to. Where two sources of one concept disagree, the source with the lower rank wins.
The tier's place in the evidence order, from 1 (most authoritative).
Cross-industry frameworks, method standards and academic papers, such as APQC's PCF, ASCM and SKOS. Support only.
Standards bodies, exchanges, registries, regulators and agencies, such as API, the Energy Institute, CME Group, GLEIF, CFTC, EIA, EPA and FASB.
MPC's filings and public materials, as read into business_architecture/reference/mpc/.
Industry standard, and analysis of publicly available filings from peers (U.S. refiners), as read into business_architecture/reference/industry-view/.

The process map, value streams, data product portfolio and office lanes in business_architecture/, the decision owner's approved definitions and measure list, and the source author's recorded answers.
A rule for an agent that answers from the graph: what it may answer without reading a table or inventing a formula, or what it must refuse.
The two kinds of consumer rule.

The binding a catalog row uses to point at a Named KPI: the data product that publishes a measure's values points at the measure's IRI. Both must already be defined: the measure with its kind in the kpi module, and the data product in the data-product module. The values stay in the data product's platform.
A property the rule rests on: one an answer reads, or whose absence makes a refusal necessary.
The agent may answer from the graph alone.
The agent must refuse, and say where the answer lives instead.
The definition, name, aliases and kind of any concept, measure, data product, series, system or lane, read from its skos:definition, labels and kind.
Say a process owns, computes or approves a measure because the measure is placed on it. Only a certification placement says that.
Calculate a crack spread from the prices of its crude and product legs. The official series is the published one; a homemade crack is a different number.
names: Build a crack from its legs

terms.definition: Answer "who is the customer" without naming a role: sold-to, bill-to, payer or another. Customer is not a role or a KPI; the answer resolves to one role.
names: Name the customer without a role

terms.definition: Call a tracker, report or report column a KPI, or call a KPI candidate a KPI. A tracker has no grain, and a KPI needs a recorded decision that names its target and owner.
names: Treat a report column as the KPI

terms.definition: Calculate a measure's value from the graph, or quote a value from a source the graph does not bind to that measure. The graph holds definitions; the values are in the systems that compute them, and an agent quotes one only through the bound metric view (rule:value-through-bound-view). A basis is a description, not a formula.
names: Compute a value, or quote one from an unbound source

terms.definition: The nearby measures and series a measure is not, and how they differ.
The processes, capabilities and value streams a measure or data product sits on, and whether each placement certifies or is context.
names: Where a thing sits, and what the placement claims

terms.definition: A series' region, legs, barrels and RIN treatment, as a recipe, never as a value.
names: What a series is built from

terms.definition: Quote a measure's value taken through the metric view the graph binds to that measure, naming the view, and add the graph's context to it, such as the measure's definition, kind and what it is not.
names: Quote a value through its bound metric view

terms.definition: What a measure includes and excludes, where its source says so, and where that statement comes from.
The sources a definition cites, and which one is authoritative when they disagree.
The roles responsible, accountable, consulted and informed for a process, as the RACI assignments record them.
Whether the rule says what the agent may answer or what it must refuse.
The two things a placement can claim.
The link names a data product's owning process: the producing process, which is the subject of vs:produces and the target of dp:producedBy.
The link says only where one thing is used or placed with another. It does not say either end owns, computes or approves the other.
What a placing property claims: certification (the link names the owning process of a data product) or context (the link says only where one thing is used or placed with another).
What a measure is, before anyone computes it: its meaning, kind, grain, basis and the processes it informs. A definition, never a value: the systems that compute the measure hold its values.
The eight kinds a measure in the kpi module can be, assigned by the decision of 2026-10-18's five tests.
The measures the kpi module defines: the planning team's measures and the measures MPC publishes.
How the measure is formed, in words: its numerator, its denominator and its unit. A description, not a formula the ontology computes.
Why the measure has its kind, in one or two sentences.
The number of the test, from 1 to 5, in the decision of 2026-10-18's rule that assigned the measure's kind.

The references the measure is asked against: plans, forecasts, plan versions or history. For a plan-variance diagnostic the comparison is part of the measure. For any other kind it is a way of asking for the same measure, not a second measure.
The time and dimension the measure is stated at, for example daily by refinery.
A process the measure informs. The link is context for where the measure is used, not a certification that the process owns or computes it.
True when industry practice and public information make the measure a strong KPI candidate. It becomes a KPI only by a recorded decision that names its target and owner.
An event raised when a condition is met, for someone to notice or act on.
A value computed from market prices and the planning model to start or rank a decision, with no performance target.
A measure the business names as one of the few measures of a stated objective, with a target and an accountable owner.
An external price, spread or benchmark that the region cannot influence.
A capability request on the measure list that is not a measure, parked for a later phase.
A recurring performance measure of a unit, asset or flow, watched by exception.
Actual results against a plan, forecast, plan version or history, for one period.
A list, status or schedule of activities and dates, with no formula, unit or time grain.
The kind of measure, from the measure-kind code list. Being a KPI is one kind: a designation with a target and an owner, not a property of the formula.
A nearby measure that people take for this one but that means something else. The skos:scopeNote says how they differ.
Plans product supply, demand, transport and inventory across the distribution network.
Builds and submits the mid-term plan, compares it with the short-term plans and history, and sequences turnarounds and capital evaluations.
Plans the prompt month for the region's refineries from the latest schedule, and watches hourly and daily execution against it.
Builds the short-term refinery LP plan and hands it to refinery planning, and checks month-to-date performance against it.
The months a planning persona plans for, counted from the current month M.
The plan a planning persona builds or works from.
The measure MPC publishes that is closest to this one, by its number in mpc-performance-measures-evidence.md, or none.
A planning persona that uses the measure. A persona is a role, not a person.
What the measure leaves out, in business words, as its source states it.
What the measure counts, in business words, as its source states it.
Where the population statements come from.
One of the four office lanes of the trading organization.
The four office lanes of the trading organization: front office, middle office, back office and operations. The lanes are not declared disjoint.

Administrative and operational completion of the trade lifecycle: settlements, invoicing and netting, accounting and sub-ledger management, regulatory reporting, dispute resolution, and record-keeping.
Revenue-generating, market-facing functions of the trading organization: trading and deal execution, forecasting, pre-trade analysis, bidding strategy, and customer/counterparty engagement.

Control and analytical layer between front and back office: monitors market and credit risk and exposure, validates captured trades, calculates P&L, manages confirmations and scenario modelling, and enforces risk limits, controls, and compliance.
Physical supply chain execution supporting the traded book: scheduling, movement actualization, feedstock and product inventory management, transportation, and terminal operations.
The office lane the process map places a process in. Only the node that names a lane has one; its children do not inherit it.

A named logical data model exported from a data modelling tool, such as ER Studio Data Architect: a set of entities, their attributes, keys and relationships, designed one level above the tables a data platform builds. Each model is one individual of this class, and the entities of its export belong to it.

The concept, class or code list of the party module that the entity holds data about, such as a customer account, or a code list such as the dealer classes for a lookup table that holds the whole list. Asserted only where the entity's name and description make the link clear; a doubtful link goes to the decision owner instead.
The platform table or data product of the data-product module that builds the entity on the data platform. An entity with none has no recorded implementation.

The logical model an entity of an export belongs to. The subject is the modelling tool's own entity IRI, found from the tool's identifier of the entity at each build; the value is a logical model. Every entity of a model has exactly one.

The system whose records the entity holds data from: a system of the system module, or a customer system of the party module, which says where the two are the same system. It is drafted from the entity's name.
A published price that a series is built from: a crude marker, a refined-product benchmark at a named market, or a compliance cost such as the RVO.
The kinds of benchmark price a series is built from.

One published series of a market measure, identified by what it is built from: its region, its crude and product legs and their ratio, and what it leaves out. Two series of the same measure are different series when any of these differ.
One part of a series' recipe: a benchmark and the number of barrels of it.

A named market price that a pricing measure of the kpi module presents, as the decision owner's pricing views report it: a product price at a market, a crude differential, a futures settlement, or a renewables or NGL price. A definition, never a price.
The product market regions of MPC Economics' published 3-2-1 crack series: USGC, Chicago, Group 3 (Tulsa), LA, PNW and SLC. They are price markets, not MPC's refining regions.
MPC's three refining regions, by the names MPC uses.
The benchmark series, benchmark prices and market prices the market-data module defines.
Where the complete list of a measure's series is: a view and the columns that identify, name and group each series, with the rows' filter. The module names only examples; the view lists them all.
The number of barrels of the benchmark in the recipe, as in the 3 and 2 and 1 of a 3-2-1 crack spread. A ratio, not a price.
The benchmark price the leg uses.
A published per-gallon compliance cost, such as the RVO, that an Ex-RVO crack deducts from each product barrel.
A published crude oil price that a crack spread uses for its crude leg.
A published refined-product price at a named market, used for a crack spread's product legs.
The ANS crude price, the crude marker of MPC's West Coast crack spread.
The Chicago CBOB gasoline price, a benchmark price in MPC's marketing areas.
The Chicago ULSD price, a benchmark price in MPC's marketing areas.
The Los Angeles CARB diesel price, a benchmark price in MPC's marketing areas.
The Los Angeles CARBOB gasoline price, a benchmark price in MPC's marketing areas.
The MEH crude price, the crude marker of MPC's Gulf Coast crack spread.
The gasoline input of MPC Economics' Gulf Coast crack series.
The diesel input of MPC Economics' Gulf Coast crack series.
The Renewable Volume Obligation cost per gallon, the same input in every region; an Ex-RVO series deducts it from each product barrel.
The gasoline input of MPC Economics' Group 3 crack series.
The crude input of MPC Economics' Gulf Coast crack series, named an MEH crack.
The gasoline input of MPC Economics' Chicago crack series.
The diesel input of MPC Economics' Chicago crack series.
The crude input of MPC Economics' LA crack series, named an ANS crack.
The crude input of MPC Economics' Chicago and Group 3 crack series, both named WTI cracks.
The diesel input of MPC Economics' Group 3 crack series.

This process contains the sub-processes to establish and execute commercial contracts, licenses, agreements with customers and/or partners.  It incorporates the steps of drafting, approving, executing and sending the commercial contract with the commercial terms and conditions to be included in commercial contracts.

This process contains the sub-processes to assess the customer's creditworthiness in order to establish the customer's credit limit and assign a risk code (e.g., risk rating and risk category). The credit assessment is largely based on customer financials and third party credit agency scores.
This process contains the sub-processes associated with collecting overdue receivables thru engagement with customers.
This process includes the sub-processes associated with initiating and managing customer accounts where legal action has or is to be taken to address unpaid balances.

This process contains the sub-processes to initiate, issue and close quotes and renewals when requested by, or targeted to the customer for a particular product and service. It also includes managing responses to RFPs and creating sale contracts.

This process contains the sub-processes associated with maintaining the underlying policies associated with commercial terms (e.g., payment terms, discounts, rebates).  It aims at establishing a common standard understanding of the commercial terms to establish contracts between seller, partners, and buyer.

This process contains the sub-processes to maintain the customer credit policies and aims at driving the strategic and tactical use of credit as a tool to support the sales strategy while managing credit related losses (i.e., bad debt) to the desired target.

This process contains the sub-processes associated with the creation of a new customer and/or maintenance of current customers master data attributes.  The customer master retains the fundamental attributes that enable key activities across Orders & Fulfilment (e.g., order validation), Billing (e.g., invoice generation) and other areas across O2C (e.g., taxation).

This process contains the sub-processes associated with managing and maintaining attributes associated with prices and discounts.  The maturity level of this environment influences directly the volume and impact of price related disputes.

The process contains the sub-processes associated with creating and maintaining all the product related attributes and is a key component supporting the order in-take supporting validation and accuracy.

This process contains the sub-processes to populate and maintain key master data attributes that supports the effective and accurate calculation of indirect tax - which is usually maintained within a bolt-on environment outside of the customer and product master data environment.

This process contains the sub-processes to manage the rules and hierarchy associated with functioning of workflows across O2C - and it is fundamental to support enforcement of controls and approval hierarchy.

The process contains the sub-processes associated with fulfilling orders.  It is largely focused on the interactions between the order management team and the fulfillment team in support of accuracy, timeliness, and exceptions resolution.

This process contains the sub-processes associated with managing product returns - including setting returns budget for return to stock (RTS) products as well as receiving, approving, and creating the return authorization (RA) across all return types (e.g., RTS, defective, shipment integrity).
This process contains the sub-processes associated with identifying and addressing unapplied receipts.  This includes activities associated with identifying, evaluating and addressing exceptions.

This process contains the sub-processes to monitor, evaluate, and release credit order blocks - i.e., orders “held” in queue due to systematic holds triggered by credit based violations usually set based on the credit risk category (a customer master attribute).  It also triggers potential reviews and revisions of the credit limit.
This process includes the sub-processes associated with negotiated settlements with customers who are in an overdue position.  Reviews and approvals are sometimes part of the settlement process.
This process contains the sub-processes to review, approve, issue, and manage customer / consumer related appeasement / concessions.

This process contains the sub-processes associated with performing reconciliations and settlements largely associated with highly transactional environments where high frequency reconciliations (e.g., daily) are a key component of managing and conducting business (e.g., sales audit, credit card settlements, rebate settlements).

This process contains the sub-processes to review contracts to determine appropriate GAAP treatment and book the entries including revenue recognition, accruals (e.g., shipped but not billed) and to calculate, evaluate and record revenue impacting provisions or reserves (e.g., product returns, post-invoice discounts).

This process contains the sub-processes associated with calculating, evaluating, and determining proper bad debt reserve levels and recording respective accrual to bring bad debt reserves to required levels

This process contains the sub-processes associated with the receiving of customer payment information - usually through a bank lock-box interface.  This is a fundamental input to support the cash application process (i.e., apply receipts).

This process contains the sub-processes associated with receiving of customer remittance information to support effective and efficient execution of cash application activities (i.e., apply receipts).

This process contains the sub-processes to receive and validate a customer query / claim. A customer query / claim is usually associated with perceived errors associated with products (e.g., product type, quantity of products) which are largely classified as “shipment integrity” claims or pricing and discounts.
This process contains the sub-processes to reconcile indirect taxes and identify and resolve unreconciled items.

This process contains the sub-processes to review the existing customers' creditworthiness to revise the customer's credit limit and risk code.  The credit assessment is conducted based on information from customer financials, third party credit agencies and past order / credit history with the organization.

This process contains the sub-processes associated with analyzing valid claims and deductions with the purpose of identifying the root cause and inform upstream processes to take corrective action.  This is a fundamental capability needed to support continuous improvement across the end-to-end O2C process.

terms.definition: This process contains the sub-processes to monitor the customer order status and respond to their inquiries including backorder management.  Additionally, the process also includes the use of the order book as a predictor of product demand and revenues.

This process contains the sub-processes to initiate, analyze, and approve deductions. Deductions are initiated by the customer upon payment and are consequently managed and monitored. A valid and approved deduction requires no action while an invalid or rejected deduction triggers the action of a charge back to the customer.

This process group houses the processes involved in the creation, distribution, and management of billings.
This process group houses the processes involved in the close of the sub ledger, including rev rec, AR and revenue related provisions, and reconciliations.
This process group houses the processes involved in executing and managing collections - including short-term forecast.
This process group houses the processes involved in assessing, measuring, and managing credit risk. It also includes maintaining policies and analyzing portfolio credit risk.

This process group houses the processes involved in executing and managing disputes (i.e., claims and deductions) - including the analysis associated with identifying root cause and supporting upstream continuous improvement.

This process group houses processes involved with the management and maintenance of key master data environments (i.e., Customer, Price & Discount, Product, and Tax) that are fundamental to enable the transactions across the end-to-end O2C process.

This process group houses the processes involved in key components of order management (i.e., capture & validation, allocation & release, monitoring and changing orders) and fulfillment.  In addition, it also addresses reverse orders (i.e., returns) and the analytics deployed across the order book.

This process group houses the processes involved with supporting and executing commercial transactions (i.e., policies, terms & contracts, financing & payment methods, quotes & renewals) along with managing the revenue plan and analyzing customer profitability.

This process group houses the processes involved in the execution of receiving and applying payments, settling other tender type transactions (e.g., credit cards), and performing high frequency reconciliations (e.g., daily) in the course of the business.
